names.name: πήγανον
names.note: Garden, mountain and wild rue; garden R. graveolens/chalepensis, mountain kind R. montana.

names.name: Garden-Rue
names.note: Garden rue, herb of grace.

names.name: ἀρνόγλωσσον
names.note: Two kinds: greater plantain and small narrow-leaved (ribwort); standard.

names.name: Plantain
names.note: Common plantain of paths and meadows.

names.name: πευκέκδανον
names.note: Peukedanon; Berendes Haarstrang (Peucedanum).

names.name: Sow-Fennel, Or Hog’S-Fennel
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἶρις Ἰλλυρική
names.note: Berendes/Beck: Illyrian orris; sword-like leaves, variously coloured flowers, fragrant rhizome. Exact species debated (I. germanica/pallida).

names.name: ἴρινον
names.note: Oil perfumed with Illyrian iris root.

names.name: Flower-De-Luce
names.note: Garden flower-de-luce, not described; flaggy and dwarf kinds; orris iris most likely.

names.name: πεντέφθλλον
names.note: Five-leaved herb; standard identification.

names.name: Five-Fingered Grass
names.note: Five-fingered grass = cinquefoil; standard identification.

names.name: κέστρον τὸ καλούμενον
names.note: Roman vettonica named in the text; standard identification.

names.name: γίνεται δὲ καὶ
names.note: Kestros psychotrophos = betony; standard identification.

names.name: Wood Betony
names.note: Wood betony; standard identification.

names.name: καὶ ὁ τροχίτης
names.note: Trochites/sykites from dried black figs, made in Cyprus.

names.name: σῦκα
names.note: Fresh and dried figs, wild-fig sap, fig-wood lye; standard.

names.name: The Fig-Tree
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: γλήχων
names.note: Glechon, well-known herb; uncontroversial.

names.name: Pennyroyal
names.note: Common pennyroyal, creeping mint.

names.name: κράμβη ἥμερος
names.note: Cultivated cabbage; standard.

names.name: Cabbages And Coleworts
names.note: Cabbages and coleworts; standard identification.

names.name: καλαμίνθη
names.note: Three kinds; Berendes: two Mentha spp. plus Thymus calamintha; mountain kind usually calamint.

names.name: οἶνος καλαμινθίτης
names.note: Kalaminthe (calamint), glechon (pennyroyal), abrotonon (southernwood) wines made like thyme wine.

names.name: Calamint, Or Mountain-Mint
names.note: Small hoary pungent mint-like herb with pale bluish flowers on dry heaths; calamint group.

names.name: χαμαίπιτυς
names.note: Creeping pine-scented herb; three kinds described: first A. chamaepitys, others subsp. chia and A. iva.

names.name: χαμαιπιτύινος ὁμοίως σκευάζεται
names.note: Chamaipitys = ground-pine; standard identification.

names.name: Ground Pine, Or Chamepitys
names.note: Low hairy plant with three-cleft leaves, pine scent: Chamaepitys.

names.name: ἀψίνθιον
names.note: Pontic/Cappadocian wormwood; chapter adds seriphon (sea wormwood).

names.name: ἀψινθίτης δὲ ποικίλως σκευάζεται
names.note: Apsinthion = wormwood; standard identification.

names.name: Wormwood
names.note: Common wormwood main; sea wormwood and Roman wormwood also treated.

names.name: δάφνινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil from ripe laurel berries.

names.name: δάφνη
names.note: Narrow- and broad-leaved daphne are both bay laurel; standard identification.

names.name: The Bay Tree
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: μολόχη
names.note: Garden and wild mallow; common mallow usual reading.

names.name: Mallows And Marshmallows
names.note: Common mallow plus marshmallow (Althaea officinalis), both described.

names.name: πράσιον
names.note: Prasion; Berendes Marrubium vulgare.

names.name: ὁ διὰ πρασίου
names.note: Prasion = white horehound; standard identification.

names.name: Horehound
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἡδύοσμον
names.note: Hedyosmon/minthe, garden mint; spearmint usual identification.

names.name: Mint
names.note: Spear or heart mint explicitly described.

names.name: σινάπινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil from mustard seed; ancient sinapi includes white and black mustard.

names.name: σίναπι
names.note: Mustard seed; white versus black mustard is debated.

names.name: Mustard
names.note: Rough beaked pods with round yellowish seed fit white mustard; black mustard also possible.

names.name: σφονδύλιον
names.note: Plane-like leaves, broad winged seeds; Berendes Bärenklau (Heracleum).

names.name: Cow Parsnips
names.note: Large rough pinnate leaves; cow parsnip is hogweed.

names.name: πάνκες Ἡράκλειον
names.note: Herakleion panakes yielding opopanax gum; Berendes Ferula opopanax / Opopanax chironium.

names.name: All-Heal
names.note: Hercules's All-heal / Opopane-wort; pinnate hairy leaves, tall stalk, yellow umbels fit Opopanax chironium.

names.name: μήκων
names.note: Garden poppy, source of opion and mekonion; opium poppy.

names.name: Poppy
names.note: White and black garden poppies = P. somniferum; corn rose = P. rhoeas.

names.name: πολύγονον ἄρρεν
names.note: Male polygonon, many-jointed creeping herb; standard identification.

names.name: Knotgrass
names.note: Knotgrass is the standard name for Polygonum aviculare.

names.name: ἄγχουσα
names.note: Anchusa with red dye root; standard identification.

names.name: Alkanet
names.note: Orchanet/Spanish bugloss/Enchusa = dye-root Alkanna tinctoria; Culpeper's English localities suggest confusion with a native borage.

names.name: ἁβροτόνινον
names.note: Oil of abrotonon (southernwood); species-level identity of abrotonon slightly debated.

names.name: ἁβρότονον
names.note: Male and female kinds; male usually A. abrotanum, female debated.

names.name: Southern Wood
names.note: Southernwood.

names.name: ὀρίγανος Ἡρακλεωτική
names.note: Berendes Origanum heracleoticum (= O. vulgare subsp. hirtum).

names.name: ἡ δὲ ἀγριορίγανος
names.note: Berendes Origanum vulgare var. album; dill-like umbels, white flowers.

names.name: οἶνος ὀριγανίτης διʼ
names.note: Origanon Herakleotikon = O. heracleoticum, now Origanum vulgare subsp. hirtum.

names.name: Wind Marjoram
names.note: Called Origanum, wild or field marjoram.

names.name: ἀνδράχνη
names.note: Cooling astringent pot-herb; standard.

names.name: Purslain
names.note: Garden purslane salad herb.

names.name: πυροί
names.note: Pyros: free-threshing wheat; bread and durum wheat not distinguished in the text.

names.name: ἄμμλον ὠνόμασται διὰ τὸ χωρὶς μύλου κατασκευάζεσθαι
names.note: Starch made without milling from 'setanios' wheat by soaking and treading; soft wheat assumed.

names.name: Wheat
names.note: All kinds of wheat; main one bread wheat.

names.name: σεῦτλον
names.note: Black and white beet; standard.

names.name: Beets
names.note: White and red beets; standard identification.

names.name: κισσός
names.note: Ivy with white, black and helix kinds; uncontroversial genus and species.

names.name: Ivy
names.note: Climbing on trees and church walls; the only native English ivy.

names.name: κάρυα βασιλικά
names.note: Royal or Persian nuts = walnut; standard.

names.name: The Wallnut Tree
names.note: Walnut tree.

names.name: ἀναγαλλίς
names.note: Two kinds differing by flower: red (male) and blue (female) pimpernel.

names.name: Pimpernel
names.note: Square trailing stalks, sessile paired leaves, single flowers: scarlet pimpernel.

names.name: μελισσόφυλλον
names.note: Melissophyllon, loved by bees; uncontroversial.

names.name: Balm
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κοκκυμηλέα
names.note: Plum tree; Damascene dried plums; wild plums also mentioned.

names.name: Plums
names.note: Plums.

names.name: χαμαίρωψ ἢ χαμαίδρυς ἢ λινόδρυς
names.note: Oak-like small leaves; Sprengel/Sibthorp T. chamaedrys, Fraas T. lucidum.

names.name: καὶ ὁ χαμαιδρυίτης
names.note: Chamaidrys = wall germander; standard identification.

names.name: Germander
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κοτυληδών
names.note: Cup-shaped round leaves on short stalk; navelwort.

names.name: Kidneywort, Or Wall Pennyroyal, Or Wall Pennywort
names.note: Peltate saucer-like leaves on walls: wall pennywort/navelwort.

names.name: κύαμος Ἑλλην ικὸς
names.note: Kyamos Hellenikos = Greek (broad) bean; uncontroversial.

names.name: Beans
names.note: Garden beans of 17th-century England; standard identification.

names.name: κρόμυον
names.note: Standard identification; long, round, yellow and white onions distinguished.

names.name: Onions
names.note: Garden onion.

names.name: σκόροδον
names.note: Cultivated and wild garlic; Egyptian single-headed form; uncontroversial.

names.name: Garlick
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἄσπληνος
names.note: Asplenon/skolopendrion with lobed leaves, rusty beneath; Berendes Ceterach officinarum.

names.name: Spleenwort, Ceterach, Or Heart’S Tongue
names.note: Fronds lobed to midrib, rusty scales beneath, on walls: Ceterach.

names.name: κενταύρειον τὸ λεπτὸν
names.note: Small centaury, hypericum-like, of moist places; uncontroversial.

names.name: The Ordinary Small Centaury
names.note: Small centaury; standard identification.

names.name: μάραθον
names.note: Marathon; uncontroversial.

names.name: καὶ μαραθίτης δὲ
names.note: Marathon (fennel), anethon (dill), petroselinon wines made alike.

names.name: Fennel
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κριθή
names.note: Barley (standard); includes barley water (ptisane).

names.name: ζῦθος
names.note: Beer made from barley.

names.name: κοῦρμι
names.note: Barley drink used instead of wine (Iberia, Britain).

names.name: Barley
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἑλένιον
names.note: Standard identification (Berendes, Beck); large rough leaves, yellow flowers, aromatic root.

names.name: ὁ δὲ νεκταρίτης
names.note: Nektarites from helenion (elecampane); standard identification.

names.name: Elecampane
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ξυρίς
names.note: Wild iris, Roman gladiolus; standard identification.

names.name: Stinking Gladwin
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: μορέα
names.note: Morea or sykaminon: mulberry (black mulberry in antiquity); standard.

names.name: The Mulberry-Tree
names.note: Mulberry grown in 17th-century England was the black mulberry.

names.name: σαμψούχινον
names.note: Multi-herb oil named after sampsuchon (marjoram); mapped to eponymous ingredient.

names.name: ἀμαράκινον
names.note: Amarakon equals sampsuchon (marjoram) per Diosc. 3.39; multi-ingredient unguent.

names.name: σάμψουχον κράτιστον τὸ
names.note: Sampsuchon/amarakon of Cyzicus and Cyprus; Berendes Origanum majorana.

names.name: Sweet Marjoram
names.note: Garden sweet marjoram; pot marjoram mentioned (O. onites).

names.name: ἐρέβινθος ὁ ἥμερος
names.note: Erebinthos hemeros = cultivated chickpea; uncontroversial.

names.name: Chick-Pease, Or Cicers
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: λευκόϊον γνώριμον. ἐστι δʼ αὐτοῦ διαφορὰ ἐν τῷ ἄνθει
names.note: Leukoion; yellow kind used medicinally = Cheiranthus cheiri (Berendes); other colours Matthiola.

names.name: Wall Flowers, Or Winter Gilli-Flowers
names.note: Single yellow wild wallflowers on walls.

names.name: ἰσάτις
names.note: Dyers' plant with plantain-like leaves; uncontroversial.

names.name: ἰσάτις ἀγρία
names.note: Tongue-shaped hanging pods, yellow flowers; Berendes: wild variety of Isatis tinctoria.

names.name: Woad
names.note: Woad, bluish plantain-like leaves.

names.name: μῆον Ἀθαμαντικόν
names.note: Standard identification; Linnaean epithet derives from Dioscorides' 'Athamantic meon'.

names.name: Spignel, Or Spikenard
names.note: Hair-fine leaves, aromatic root: spignel/baldmoney.

names.name: πετροσέλινον
names.note: Macedonian cliffs, ammi-like seed; Fraas parsley, Sprengel Athamanta macedonica (= Bubon macedonicum).

names.name: Parsley
names.note: Garden parsley.

names.name: κεράσια
names.note: Cherries and cherry-tree gum; sweet or sour cherry not distinguished.

names.name: The Cherry-Tree
names.note: Orchard cherries, sweet and sour, not described; sweet = P. avium, sour = P. cerasus.

names.name: μυρσίνη ἀγρία
names.note: Myrtle-like sharp leaves with central red berry; Berendes: Ruscus aculeatus.

names.name: Butcher’S Broom
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: οἰνάνθινον
names.note: Oil of oenanthe, the fragrant flower of the (wild) grapevine.

names.name: γλεύκινον
names.note: Multi-ingredient oil prepared with grape must; mapped to eponymous ingredient.

names.name: ἀμπέλου οἰνοφόρου τὰ
names.note: Cultivated wine vine, leaves and tendrils; grapevine.

names.name: ἄμπελος ἀγρία διττή
names.note: Two wild vines; wild grape (Vitis vinifera subsp. sylvestris).

names.name: σταφυλή᾿ ἡ μὲν
names.note: Fresh and stored grapes and raisins; fruit of the grapevine.

names.name: ο ἰνάνθη καλεῖται
names.note: Flowering clusters of wild vine, dried and stored; Vitis vinifera.

names.name: ὀμφάκιον
names.note: Juice of unripe grapes pressed before the Dog Star.

names.name: οἶνοι
names.note: Wines in general; product of the grapevine.

names.name: ὄξος ψύχει καὶ
names.note: Wine vinegar; product of the grapevine.

names.name: ὀ μφακόμελι δὲ σκευάζεται τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον
names.note: Juice of unripe grapes (omphax) with honey.

names.name: ρἰνάνθινος δὲ σκευάζεται οὕτως
names.note: Dried flowers of wild vine (oinanthe), i.e. Vitis vinifera subsp. sylvestris.

names.name: τρύγα δὲ παραλημπτέον
names.note: Tryx: lees of old wine, also burnt.

names.name: τέφρα κληματίνη δύναμιν
names.note: Tephra klematine: ash of vine shoots.

names.name: The Vine
names.note: Vine.

names.name: Εὐπατόριος
names.note: Single woody hairy stem, divided leaves, burred seed; agrimony.

names.name: Agrimony
names.note: Standard identification of herbal agrimony.

names.name: ἀνεμώνη
names.note: Cultivated and wild anemones with differently coloured flowers; main kind A. coronaria.

names.name: Anemone
names.note: Garden windflowers sown by florists, not described; 17th-century garden anemones mainly A. coronaria and A. hortensis.

names.name: ἀνήθινον
names.note: Oil steeped with dill flowers.

names.name: ἀνήθου ξηροῦ τῆς
names.note: Anethon; uncontroversial.

names.name: Dill
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἄσαρον
names.note: Ivy-like rounded leaves, flower between leaves at root, fragrant rootlets: asarabacca (standard).

names.name: ἀσαρίτης
names.note: Asaron = asarabacca; standard identification.

names.name: ὁ διὰ τῆς ἀγρίας νάρδου
names.note: Dsc 1.10 gives 'wild nard' as synonym of asaron, but separate chapter from asarites; uncertain.

names.name: Asarabacca
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἀσπάραγος πετραῖος
names.note: Rock or prickly asparagus (myakanthos): spiny wild Mediterranean asparagus.

names.name: Prickly Asparagus, Or Sperage
names.note: Heading = Mediterranean prickly sperage (A. acutifolius), but the wild Gloucestershire locality suggests feral A. officinalis.

names.name: σταφυλῖνος ἄγριος
names.note: Wild staphylinos with central purple floret; Berendes Daucus carota var. silvestris.

names.name: Carrots
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἡλιοτρόπιον τὸ μέγα
names.note: Scorpion-tail inflorescence; Berendes: Heliotropium villosum or H. europaeum.

names.name: Turnsole, Or Heliotropium
names.note: Greater turnsole: hoary annual, white flowers on curled spike, Mediterranean.

names.name: θρίδαξ ἥμερος
names.note: Garden lettuce; wild lettuce with opium-like latex also treated.

names.name: Lettuce
names.note: Garden salad lettuce.

names.name: σούσινον
names.note: Susinum/leirinon: oil of white lily flowers with aromatics.

names.name: κρίνον
names.note: Krinon/leirion, garland flower, source of susinon oil; uncontroversial.

names.name: White Lilies
names.note: White garden lily of 17th-century England is Lilium candidum.

names.name: Λυσιμάχειος
names.note: Willow-like leaves, purple or golden flowers, wet places; probably conflates Lysimachia and Lythrum.

names.name: Loosestrife Or Willow-Herb
names.note: Common yellow loosestrife, tall with leaves in pairs or whorls.

names.name: λεύκη
names.note: Leuke = white poplar, paired with aigeiros (black poplar); standard.

names.name: The Poplar Tree
names.note: White and black poplar both described.

names.name: ἐρυθρόδανον ἐρευθέδανον
names.note: Red dye root, wild and cultivated kinds; standard identification (Berendes, Beck).

names.name: Madder
names.note: Garden madder: rough square trailing stems, whorled leaves.

names.name: σύμφυτον ἄλλο
names.note: Hairy angular hollow stem, decurrent leaves, yellowish flowers, itchy hairs; comfrey.

names.name: Comfrey
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: παρθένιιον
names.note: Coriander-like leaves, white rays; Fraas Matricaria parthenium, Sprengel M. chamomilla.

names.name: Feverfew Or Featherfew
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: βήχιον
names.note: Bechion, cough herb, smoke inhaled; Berendes Tussilago farfara.

names.name: Coltsfoot
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἴον
names.note: Purple fragrant ion with ivy-like leaves; sweet violet.

names.name: Violets
names.note: Tame and wild violets.

names.name: ἄκανθος
names.note: Akanthos/paideros of gardens, broad glossy leaves; standard A. mollis.

names.name: Brank Ursine
names.note: Bear's-breech/Acanthus nursed in gardens; white hooded flowers; standard identification.

names.name: φυλλῖτις
names.note: Lapathon-like leaves with sori beneath; Berendes Scolopendrium officinale.

names.name: Hart’S-Tongue
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: χελιδόνιον μέγα
names.note: Saffron-coloured acrid sap, swallow lore; uncontroversial.

names.name: Celandine
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: σέρις
names.note: Wild seris (pikris) and two garden kinds: endive and chicory group.

names.name: Endive
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: φακὸς ὁ ἐπὶ
names.note: Lentil-like growth on stagnant water; duckweed.

names.name: Duck’S Meat
names.note: Duck's meat = duckweed; standard identification.

names.name: αἶπα ἡ γινομένη
names.note: Aira growing among wheat = darnel; standard identification.

names.name: Darnel
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: λειχὴν ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν πετρῶν
names.note: Moss-like growth on wet rocks, used for lichen (skin); liverwort (Berendes).

names.name: Liverwort
names.note: Flat thallus on damp shady ground with small stalked star-like heads (receptacles) fits Marchantia.

names.name: μυρρίς
names.note: Hemlock-like plant with fragrant, sweet edible root; sweet cicely.

names.name: Sweet Chervil, Or Sweet Cicely
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἀνωνίς
names.note: Berendes Ononis antiquorum (now O. spinosa subsp. antiquorum).

names.name: Rest Harrow, Or Cammock
names.note: Woody twigs armed with short sharp thorns: restharrow (GBIF includes O. repens as subsp. procurrens).

names.name: ψύλλιον
names.note: Fleawort; Plantago psyllium (=P. afra).

names.name: Flea-Wort
names.note: Flea-like shining seed in chaffy heads, garden-grown; Psyllium; second seaside sort uncertain.

names.name: ἀπίτης σκευάζεται ὁμοίως
names.note: Pear wine; also wines of carob (keration), medlar (mespilon) and service-berry (oa).

names.name: ἄπιος
names.note: Many kinds of pear; achras = wild pear (P. spinosa).

names.name: The Pear Tree
names.note: Pear trees.

names.name: σόγχος
names.note: Two kinds: spinier (S. asper) and tender edible (S. oleraceus); standard.

names.name: Sow Thistle
names.note: Sow thistles.

names.name: πτελέα
names.note: Ptelea = elm; field elm the common Mediterranean species.

names.name: The Elm Tree
names.note: Common English elm (U. procera, now in U. minor), not described; wych elm also widespread.

names.name: περιστέριον
names.note: Upright peristereon of watery places with cut whitish leaves; vervain (Berendes).

names.name: Vervain
names.note: Common vervain with square branched stalks.

names.name: ἰξός
names.note: Birdlime from round berries of ixia with box-like leaves, i.e. mistletoe.

names.name: Misselto
names.note: Woody parasite with paired leaves on tree branches.

names.name: ἀνδράφαξυς
names.note: Wild and garden orache eaten boiled; standard.

names.name: Garden Arrach
names.note: Garden arrach = garden orache; standard identification.

names.name: καρώ
names.note: Karo, known aromatic seed; standard caraway.

names.name: Carraway
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κώνειον
names.note: Jointed fennel-like stem, heavy smell; poison hemlock.

names.name: Hemlock
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: μήλινον
names.note: Oil perfumed by quinces (kydonia mela) laid over it.

names.name: ὁ μὲν οὖν κυδωνί ίτης
names.note: Kydonites/melites from quince (melon kydonion).

names.name: καὶ μηλόμελι δέ
names.note: Quinces preserved in honey.

names.name: ὑδρόμηλον δὲ σκευάζεται
names.note: Quince honey diluted with water.

names.name: The Quince Tree
names.note: Quince tree described.

names.name: ἀπαρίνη
names.note: Rough clinging stems, whorled leaves; Berendes Galium aparine.

names.name: Cleavers
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: γάλιον
names.note: Galion, curdles milk; lady's bedstraw.

names.name: Ladies Bed-Straw
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: γλυκύρριζα
names.note: Sweet root; burr-like fruit heads described fit G. echinata; G. glabra usual identification.

names.name: Liquorice
names.note: Pinnate ash-like leaves; English-grown liquorice root.

names.name: ὑσσωπίτης δὲ ὁ
names.note: Cilician hyssopos; usually Hyssopus officinalis, some read Origanum syriacum.

names.name: Hyssop
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: βράθυ
names.note: Cypress-like, heavy-smelling, low spreading; abortifacient: savin (standard). Second, tamarisk-leaved kind uncertain.

names.name: Savine
names.note: Savine, evergreen garden shrub.

names.name: λιγυστικόν
names.note: Ligurian Apennine umbellifer, poorly described; Sprengel Levisticum officinale or Laserpitium siler.

names.name: Lovage
names.note: Large winged leaves like smallage, hollow stalks; garden lovage.

names.name: λιθόσπερμον
names.note: Stony white seeds; standard Lithospermum officinale.

names.name: Gromel
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὑδροπέπερι
names.note: Jointed-stemmed plant by still water with peppery taste; Berendes: Wasserpfeffer.

names.name: Arssmart
names.note: Hot arssmart = water-pepper; mild/dead arssmart = P. maculosa.

names.name: στρούθιον
names.note: Wool-washers' root (saponin); Berendes: Seifenkraut; Gypsophila struthium also proposed.

names.name: Sopewort, Or Bruisewort
names.note: Creeping jointed roots, plantain-like ribbed leaves: soapwort.

names.name: ἱπποσέλινον
names.note: Hipposelinon/olusatrum, black seed; Fraas Smyrnium olusatrum.

names.name: Alexander
names.note: Standard identification of alexanders.

names.name: στρύχνον κηπαῖον
names.note: Edible garden strychnos; black nightshade.

names.name: Nightshade
names.note: Common nightshade with basil-like leaves and black berries.

names.name: ἀ ἀλσίνη
names.note: Mouse-ear-leaved low herb of shady groves smelling of cucumber; chickweed.

names.name: Chickweed
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: θλάσπι
names.note: Flattened disc-like 'crushed' fruit fits pennycress; Berendes prefers shepherd's purse.

names.name: Treacle Mustard
names.note: Round notched pouches, entire leaves, white flowers, garlic smell.

names.name: φοῦ
names.note: Pontic valerian with fetid nard-like root; Linnaeus named V. phu after it; V. dioscoridis also proposed.

names.name: Garden Valerian
names.note: Garden valerian with entire then pinnate leaves, thick root above ground.

names.name: στρατιώτης ὁ χιλιόφυλλος
names.note: Thousand-leaved 'soldier' wound herb with feathery leaves; yarrow.

names.name: Yarrow, Called Nose-Bleed, Milfoil And Thousand-Leal
names.note: Yarrow/milfoil.

names.name: ἔστι δὲ καὶ
names.note: Halikakkabon with fruit in a bladder-like husk; winter cherry (Physalis alkekengi).

names.name: Winter-Cherries
names.note: Winter cherry = Physalis alkekengi; standard identification.

names.name: πύρεθρος
names.note: Burning root for toothache; Berendes Anacyclus pyrethrum; 'umbel' wording questioned.

names.name: Pellitory Of Spain
names.note: Single flower white above, reddish beneath; English wild sort described is sneezewort.

names.name: ἄρκιον
names.note: Large gourd-like leaves (prosopis/arkeion); burdock.

names.name: The Burdock
names.note: Great burdock/Personata; lesser burdock equally common in England and not distinguished.

names.name: κάνναβις
names.note: Rope-fibre plant with ash-like, ill-smelling leaves; uncontroversial.

names.name: Hemp
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὀξυάκανθα
names.note: Pear-like very spiny small tree, red myrtle-sized fruit with stones: hawthorn; synonym pyrakantha suggests firethorn for some.

names.name: Hawthorn
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἐπίθυμον
names.note: Hair-like 'flower' of thyme, i.e. parasitic dodder; Berendes: Cuscuta epithymum.

names.name: Dodder Of Thyme, Epithymum, And Other Dodders
names.note: Dodder of thyme (Epithymum); other dodders included.

names.name: πτέρις
names.note: Fronds from one stock, black rhizome, vermifuge; Berendes: Aspidium filix-mas.

names.name: Fern
names.note: Male and female fern treated together; herbalists' female fern usually bracken.

names.name: οἰνάνθη
names.note: Root with many round heads; Fraas Spiraea filipendula, Sprengel Pedicularis tuberosa.

names.name: Filipendula, Or Drop-Wort
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: καπνὸς ὁ ἐν ταῖς κριθαῖς φυόμενος
names.note: Kapnos among barley, coriander-like; fumitory.

names.name: Fumitory
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: λεπίδιον
names.note: Pickled in brine; acrid vesicant leaves; usual identification as dittander.

names.name: Pepperwort, Or Dittander
names.note: Broad bluish leaves, white flowers, tall: dittander.

names.name: λινόζωστις
names.note: Male and female plants distinguished; Berendes: Bingelkraut. Text also contains RV kynokrambe chapter.

names.name: French And Dog Mercury
names.note: French mercury, annual and branched, is Mercurialis annua.

names.name: σισύμβριον
names.note: Aquatic herb tasting like kardamon, called kardamine: watercress (standard).

names.name: Water Cresses
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὠκίμινον
names.note: Oil steeped with basil (okimon) leaves.

names.name: ὤκιμον
names.note: Basil; standard.

names.name: Garden Bazil, Or Sweet Bazil
names.note: Garden or sweet basil; standard identification.

names.name: ἀκάνθιον
names.note: Cobweb-like down gathered as wool; Berendes Onopordon acanthium (perhaps O. illyricum).

names.name: Down, Or Cotton-Thistle
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: The Woollen, Or, Cotton Thistle
names.note: Woolly prickly leaves, crimson florets; duplicates Down or Cotton Thistle entry.

names.name: γλυκυσίδη
names.note: Male peony with walnut-like leaves; female with divided leaves = P. officinalis.

names.name: Male And Female Peony
names.note: Male peony (entire leaflets) = P. mascula; female = P. officinalis.

names.name: ἐλαφοβόσκον
names.note: Elaphoboskon, sweet edible root, deer food; Berendes Pastinaca sativa.

names.name: Parsnips
names.note: Garden and wild parsnip; wild described.

names.name: πετασῖτις
names.note: Large hat-like leaf on a stalk like a mushroom; butterbur.

names.name: The Butter-Bur, Or Petasitis
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κορωνόπους
names.note: Prostrate herb with cut leaves, eaten boiled: buck's-horn plantain usual reading.

names.name: Buck’S-Horn Plantain
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: πολυπόδιον
names.note: Fern on mossy rocks and oak trunks, sweet rhizome; Berendes: P. vulgare; Greek plants often P. cambricum.

names.name: Polypody Of The Oak
names.note: Winged fronds on oaks: polypody of the oak.

names.name: λιβανωτίς
names.note: Libanotis called rosmarinus by the Romans; uncontroversial.

names.name: Rosemary
names.note: Garden rosemary.

names.name: ἡριγέρων
names.note: Erigeron 'early old man' with pappus; groundsel.

names.name: Groundsel
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Maple Tree
names.note: No description; field maple is the native English maple.

names.name: ἀνδρόσακες
names.note: White leafless seashore 'herb' with apical cup = marine alga Acetabularia; Sprengel 'Tubularia acetabulum'.

names.name: καλοῦσί τινες καὶ
names.note: Achilleios sideritis: finely cut leaves, round umbel-like head, wound herb; yarrow.

names.name: ἀγήρατον
names.note: Low origanum-like herb with umbel of golden 'bubble' flowers; sweet yarrow.

names.name: Sweet Maudlin
names.note: Yellow tansy-like flower heads, narrow toothed leaves: sweet maudlin.

names.name: γναφαλλίου
names.note: White soft leaves used as stuffing; Berendes Athanasia maritima (= Otanthus maritimus).

names.name: πταρμική
names.note: Sternutatory shrublet like southernwood; Berendes: Niesgarbe; species in genus debated.

names.name: ἀκόνιτον ἕτερον
names.note: Lykoktonon from the Vestini mountains of Italy; Aconitum.

names.name: ἄκορον
names.note: Berendes/Gunther: sweet flag; iris-like narrow leaves, knotty aromatic creeping rhizome. Some propose Iris pseudacorus.

names.name: κάλαμος ἀρωματικός
names.note: Traditionally sweet flag; jointed culm with cobweb-like pith suggests an Indian aromatic grass. Debated.

names.name: ἀκορίτης δὲ καὶ ὁ ἀπὸ γλυκυρρίζης σκευάζεται ὁμοίως
names.note: Akoron (sweet flag; some read Iris pseudacorus) and glykyrrhiza (liquorice) wines.

names.name: ἀδίαντον
names.note: Coriander-like leaflets that shed water; maidenhair fern.

names.name: αἰγίλωψ
names.note: Wheat-like grass with two or three awned glumes; text also contains RV bromos (Avena).

names.name: Gout-Wort, Or Herb Gerrard
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἀείζῳον μέγα
names.note: Large evergreen succulent, scarred stems, tongue-shaped leaves; Sempervivum arboreum (Berendes).

names.name: λυχνὶς ἀγρία
names.note: Wild lychnis similar to garden one; Berendes Agrostemma githago.

names.name: Bugle
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Ladies’ Mantle
names.note: Round pleated lobed leaves: Alchemilla vulgaris aggregate.

names.name: ἄλισμα
names.note: Plantain-like leaves, thyrse of white flowers, watery places; Alisma and Damasonium both proposed.

names.name: Sauce-Alone, Or Jack-By-The-Hedge-Side
names.note: Jack-by-the-hedge with nettle-shaped leaves, white flowers.

names.name: μῶ λυ
names.note: Grass-like leaves, milk-white flowers, small bulb; Berendes lists Allium nigrum/magicum; contested.

names.name: ἀμπελόπρασον
names.note: Vineyard leek; name gives the binomial; Berendes: Weinlauch.

names.name: Cives
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: σκορδόπρασον
names.note: Large leek with garlic-like qualities; Berendes: Skorodoprason; species debated.

names.name: The Common Alder-Tree
names.note: Common alder tree; standard identification.

names.name: ἀλόη
names.note: Squill-like fleshy leaves, bitter juice from India/Arabia; A. vera usual, Socotrine A. perryi possible.

names.name: ἡ δὲ ἀγρία
names.note: Wild 'hemp' with hemp-like leaves, reddish flowers, althaia-like root; Berendes Althaea cannabina.

names.name: ἀολθαία
names.note: Wild mallow with round downy leaves, also called ebiskos (hibiscus); standard identification.

names.name: Amaranthus
names.note: Garden 'Flower Gentle/Velvet Flower' with red tufts and shining black seed; species uncertain.

names.name: βλίτον
names.note: Bland pot-herb without drug action; blite (Amaranthus blitum) standard.

names.name: Blites
names.note: White and red blites (Blitum) with beet-like leaves and tufted heads; usually referred to Amaranthus, species uncertain.

names.name: ἀμβροσία
names.note: Sprengel and Fraas Ambrosia maritima; rue-like leaves, Cappadocian garlands.

names.name: Bishop’S-Weed
names.note: Wild at Greenhithe, white umbels, cut leaves: Ammi majus; apothecaries' Ammi seed often Trachyspermum ammi.

names.name: ἄμωμον
names.note: Woody cluster-like aromatic from Armenia/Media/Pontus; identity long disputed, genus Amomum conventional.

names.name: ὄρχις
names.note: Kynos orchis with paired tubers; Berendes Orchis papilionacea or O. morio.

names.name: ἀνάγυρος
names.note: Foetid shrub; name kept by Linnaean genus; standard identification.

names.name: βούγλωσσον
names.note: Phlomos-like rough prostrate leaves; Anchusa italica (=azurea).

names.name: Angelica
names.note: Garden angelica of the herbals; wild angelica a possible alternative.

names.name: φαλάγγιον
names.note: Lily-like white flower, black seed; Dodonaeus Anthericum ramosum, Fraas Lloydia graeca; uncertain.

names.name: Chervil
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Parsley Piert, Or Parsley Break Stone
names.note: Small prostrate plant with parsley-like leaves: parsley piert.

names.name: σέλινον κηπαῖον
names.note: Garden selinon; uncontroversial.

names.name: σελινίτης
names.note: Selinon (garden) seed = celery; standard identification.

names.name: Smallage
names.note: Smallage is wild celery.

names.name: ἀγάλλοχον
names.note: Fragrant spotted wood from India/Arabia used as incense: agarwood (syn. Aquilaria agallocha).

names.name: Columbines
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κόμαρος
names.note: Thin-barked tree with stoneless 'memaikyla' fruit; standard.

names.name: Wild Tansy, Or Silver Weed
names.note: Wild tansy/silverweed.

names.name: ἀρίσαρον
names.note: Small aroid with olive-sized root; name preserved in Arisarum.

names.name: ἀριστολοχεία
names.note: Round (female), long (male), klematitis kinds: A. rotunda, A. longa L. (GBIF: A. fontanesii), A. clematitis.

names.name: Raddish, Or Horse-Raddish
names.note: Horse-radish described; garden radish (Raphanus sativus) only named.

names.name: ἀρτεμισία
names.note: Seaside wormwood-like shrub; Berendes A. arborescens and A. campestris; single-stemmed kind uncertain.

names.name: Mugwort
names.note: Leaves dark green above, white beneath; tall stalks.

names.name: ἄρον
names.note: Arum, Syrian 'louphá', unspotted leaves, edible root; species uncertain.

names.name: Cuckow-Point
names.note: Cuckoo-pint; standard identification.

names.name: Asparagus, Sparagus, Or Sperage
names.note: Garden asparagus; standard identification.

names.name: ἀσφόδελος
names.note: Common asphodel of Greece; genus certain, species debated.

names.name: Wall Rue, Or, White Maiden-Hair
names.note: Wall rue/white maidenhair is Asplenium ruta-muraria.

names.name: ἡμιονῖτις
names.note: Crescent leaf like dracontion; Sprengel/Fraas Scolopendrium hemionitis (= Asplenium sagittatum).

names.name: τριχομανές
names.note: Small fern like pteris with fine leaflets; Berendes: Streifenfarn; standard identification.

names.name: Maiden Hair
names.note: Black brittle stalks with small round leaflets: English 'common maidenhair' = Asplenium trichomanes.

names.name: ἀ στὴρ Ἀττικός
names.note: Star-like flower with yellow centre like anthemis; Aster amellus.

names.name: ποτίρριον
names.note: Woolly spiny shrub like tragacanth, gummy roots; Sprengel Astragalus poterium; others Sarcopoterium spinosum.

names.name: τραγάκανθα
names.note: Spiny shrub whose cut root yields gum tragacanth; Berendes: Astragalus species.

names.name: γλαύξ
names.note: Galactagogue seaside herb; Sprengel Astragalus glaux, Fraas Senebiera coronopus (Berendes); speculative.

names.name: κατανάγκη ἡ μέν
names.note: Two kinds; dried pods curve like a kite's claws; legume such as Astragalus hamosus proposed.

names.name: σαρκοκόλλα
names.note: Tear of a Persian tree; Berendes cites Dymock: Persian Astragalus (formerly Penaea).

names.name: δαῦκος
names.note: Three kinds: Cretan = Athamanta cretensis; second Peucedanum cervaria (= Cervaria rivini); third Ammi majus (Fraas).

names.name: δαυκίτης
names.note: Daukos root; Dsc's chief (Cretan) daukos usually Athamanta cretensis.

names.name: χαμαιλέων λευκός
names.note: Ixine birdlime found at the roots; standard Atractylis (Carlina) gummifera.

names.name: ἅλιμον
names.note: Spineless coastal hedge shrub with olive-like broader leaves, eaten boiled: Atriplex halimus (standard).

names.name: στρύχνον μανικόν
names.note: Madness-causing strychnos; belladonna and Datura proposed; identity debated.

names.name: βρόμος κάλαμός ἐστι
names.note: Bromos: reed-like cereal with wheat-like leaves and nodes; standard identification oat.

names.name: Oats,
names.note: Cultivated oats.

names.name: βαλλντή
names.note: Ballote/melamprasion, square black stems; Berendes Ballota.

names.name: Winter-Rocket, Or Cresses
names.note: Winter-rocket/winter cresses with lyrate leaves.

names.name: Daisies
names.note: Not described; common daisy, with the greater (ox-eye) daisy possibly included.

names.name: Barberry
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: σίον
names.note: Aquatic umbellifer with hipposelinon-like aromatic leaves; Sium angustifolium (Berula) per Berendes.

names.name: The Birch Tree
names.note: Drooping branches suggest silver birch; downy birch not distinguished in 17th century.

names.name: Water Agrimony
names.note: Purple stalk, brownish-yellow rayless heads, seeds sticking to wool fit Bidens tripartita (water hemp agrimony).

names.name: Bistort, Or Snakeweed
names.note: Bistort/snakeweed; standard identification.

names.name: τρίφυλλον
names.note: Triphyllon/asphaltion smelling of bitumen; Berendes Asphaltklee.

names.name: χρυσόγονον
names.note: Tuberous root red inside, black outside, mullein-like flower; Bongardia named from it.

names.name: Borage And Bugloss
names.note: Borage and bugloss (Anchusa officinalis); 'Langue de Boeuf' with dandelion-like yellow heads = bristly oxtongue.

names.name: λίβανος
names.note: Frankincense from Arabia 'libanotophoros': Boswellia sacra; Indian libanos possibly B. serrata.

names.name: Moonwort
names.note: Single divided leaf with fertile spike: moonwort fern.

names.name: κράμβη ἀγρία
names.note: Coastal cliff cabbage, whiter, hairier, bitter: Aegean wild Brassica (B. cretica) or wild B. oleracea.

names.name: βουνιάς
names.note: Bounias, a turnip-like root vegetable: navew (Brassica napus) per standard glossaries.

names.name: γογγύλη
names.note: Turnip root, sprouts, seed; a wild gongyle is also described.

names.name: ἄμπελος μέλαινα
names.note: Berries turning black, root dark outside, boxwood-coloured inside; Berendes: Bryonia alba; others Tamus.

names.name: ἄμπελος λευκή
names.note: White vine (bryonia); Berendes: Bryonia cretica, Sprengel B. dioica; genus certain.

names.name: Briony, Or Wild Vine
names.note: White briony described (vine-like leaves); black briony (Tamus) = Dioscorea communis.

names.name: βούνιον
names.note: Square stem, celery-like finely cut leaves, dill-like flowers; Apiaceae, species uncertain.

names.name: οἶνος διὰ βουνίου
names.note: Bounion (Dsc 4.123) tentatively Bunium ferulaceum; identification uncertain.

names.name: Thorough Wax, Or Thorough Leaf
names.note: Perfoliate bluish leaves: thorough-wax.

names.name: πομάραθον
names.note: Big wild fennel with kachrys-like seed; Berendes: undetermined, Cachrys morisonii proposed.

names.name: λιβανωτίς
names.note: Fruiting kind yields kachrys: 'ohne Zweifel' Cachrys libanotis (Berendes); second kind Ferula nodiflora.

names.name: Marigolds
names.note: Garden marigold of English herbals is Calendula officinalis.

names.name: ἀσπάλαθος
names.note: Spiny woody shrub of Nisyros/Rhodes/Syria used by perfumers; spiny broom often proposed, identity uncertain.

names.name: σμῖλαξ λεία
names.note: Thornless ivy-leaved climber with white flowers; Berendes: Convolvulus sepium; fit is weak.

names.name: κράμβη θαλασσία
names.note: Kidney-shaped leaves on reddish ivy-like shoots, milky salty sap, strongly purgative: sea bindweed (standard).

names.name: μύαγρον
names.note: Madder-like leaves, oily fenugreek-like seed; Camelina (Berendes).

names.name: μήδιον
names.note: Large round purple flowers, 3-cubit stem, shady rocky places; campanulaceous plant proposed, uncertain.

names.name: κάππαρις
names.note: Thorny sprawling shrub with edible buds and fruit; uncontroversial.

names.name: Shepherd’S Purse
names.note: Shepherd's purse.

names.name: Coralwort
names.note: Toothwort/Dentaria with axillary bulbils, knobbed creeping root, Mayfield Sussex; fits coralroot.

names.name: Ladies-Smock, Or Cuckow-Flower
names.note: Meadow plant with pinnate leaves; lady's smock/cuckoo-flower.

names.name: ὁ δὲ μέλας
names.note: Berendes: Carthamus corymbosus L. (= Cardopatium corymbosum); umbel-like spiny inflorescence, black root.

names.name: κροκοδείλεον
names.note: Like black chamaeleon, cress-scented root; Berendes Carduus pycnocephalus; tentative.

names.name: ἀτρακτυλίς
names.note: Safflower-like thistle used as spindle; Matthiolus/Fraas Carthamus lanatus.

names.name: κνῆκος
names.note: Spiny heads with saffron-coloured flowers, seeds used as purge; Berendes: Saflor.

names.name: Chesnut Tree
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κεδρίτης δὲ γίνεται οὕτω
names.note: Kedria (cedar pitch) in must; Dsc 1.77 big kedros often read as Lebanon cedar, debated.

names.name: κέδρος
names.note: Large tree yielding kedria (cedar pitch, embalming); small spiny kedros with juniper-like berries is a Juniperus.

names.name: λωτός
names.note: Large 'lotus tree', sweet fruit bigger than pepper, wood yellows hair: Celtis australis (Berendes); Ziziphus lotus alternative.

names.name: Carduus Benedictus
names.note: Carduus benedictus; standard identification.

names.name: Star Thistle
names.note: Star thistle with spreading branches.

names.name: Blue-Bottle
names.note: Blue-bottle = cornflower; standard identification.

names.name: Knapweed
names.note: Common knapweed; scaly heads, purple florets; slightly torn leaves could also suggest greater knapweed.

names.name: ἱππόφαιστον
names.note: Prostrate fullers' thistle, no stem or flower; Fraas: Centaurea spinosa; Sprengel: Cirsium stellatum.

names.name: κεράτια
names.note: Carob pods; standard.

names.name: τηλέφιον
names.note: Berendes: Cerinthe aspera (Wachsblume); purslane-like fleshy leaves suggest Sedum/Telephium; very uncertain.

names.name: ἀκακαλλίς
names.note: Seed of an Egyptian shrub used in eye-salves; Fraas/Berendes proposed Cassia absus (chaksu seed), speculative.

names.name: Camomile
names.note: Not described; common English camomile usually Chamaemelum nobile, but Matricaria possible.

names.name: ὀνάγρα
names.note: Tall shrub, almond-like leaves, large rose-like flowers, wine-scented root; Epilobium proposed.

names.name: Arrach, Wild And Stinking
names.note: Wild stinking arrach smelling of rotten fish; standard identification.

names.name: χονδρίλη
names.note: Chicory-like slender plant with mastic-like gum on stems; second kind unidentified.

names.name: Succory, Or Chicory
names.note: Garden and wild succory with blue flowers.

names.name: κασσία
names.note: Aromatic bark traded via Arabia; usually equated with Chinese cassia (syn. C. cassia); ancient source debated.

names.name: μαλάβαθρον
names.note: Malabathrum leaf of Indian trade is generally identified with Cinnamomum tamala; Dioscorides' account partly fabulous.

names.name: μαλαβάθρινον
names.note: Unguent like nardinum with malabathrum leaf; mapped to eponymous ingredient.

names.name: κιννάμωμον
names.note: Several trade grades of cinnamon; identity of ancient cinnamomum versus modern cinnamon remains debated.

names.name: κιναμώμινον
names.note: Multi-ingredient unguent named after cinnamon; ancient cinnamon identity debated.

names.name: ἀπόκυνον
names.note: Pliant rods, heavy-smelling ivy-like leaves, milky juice, bean-like pods, kills dogs; Cynanchum erectum of Berendes (now Cionura).

names.name: Thistles
names.note: Many English thistles treated collectively without description.

names.name: The Melancholy Thistle
names.note: Hoary stalk, weakly prickly leaves, single head.

names.name: λευκάκανθα
names.note: Only cyperus-like bitter root described; Sprengel Cirsium tuberosum, Fraas Centaurea dalmatica.

names.name: κίσθος
names.note: Male purple-flowered and female white-flowered cistus; also hypocistis (Cytinus) and ledon yielding ladanum.

names.name: κολόκυνθα ἀγρία
names.note: Bitter wild gourd; Berendes: Cucumis colocynthis; uncontroversial.

names.name: κληματίς
names.note: Climbing vine with very acrid ulcerating leaves; Berendes: Clematis vitalba or C. cirrhosa.

names.name: ἄκινος ἢ ἄκονος
names.note: Basil-like, hairier, fragrant; Berendes Thymus acinos (= Clinopodium acinos).

names.name: κλινοπόδιον
names.note: Bed-foot-like whorled flowers; Berendes Clinopodium vulgare.

names.name: χαμελαίτης
names.note: Chamelaia usually Cneorum tricoccon (spurge-olive).

names.name: Scurvygrass
names.note: English scurvygrass with long-stalked fleshy leaves.

names.name: Κολχικόν
names.note: Autumn-flowering poisonous bulb of Colchis and Messenia; Colchicum.

names.name: βάλσαμον
names.note: Judaean balsam tree (opobalsamum, xylobalsamum, carpobalsamum): Commiphora gileadensis (standard).

names.name: στακτή
names.note: Oily fraction of fresh myrrh.

names.name: σμύρνα
names.note: Gum-resin of an Arabian thorny tree: myrrh (standard).

names.name: βδέλλιον
names.note: Gum-resin ('tear') of an Arabian tree; bdellium usually equated with guggul (C. wightii) or African bdellium; source species debated.

names.name: Earth Chesnuts
names.note: Earth-nuts / pig-nuts known to every child; English pignut, though Latin bulbocastanum name points to Bunium.

names.name: ἐφήμερον
names.note: Ephemeron/wild iris with lily-like leaves, small white flowers, woods; Convallaria proposed.

names.name: Lily Of The Valley
names.note: Creeping root, white bell flowers, red berries.

names.name: ἑλξίνη
names.note: Small ivy-like leaves, long twining shoots in hedges, vineyards, grain; bindweed.

names.name: δορύκνιον
names.note: Olive-like shrub on coastal rocks, rough leaves, white flower; Convolvulus and legume candidates.

names.name: σκαμμωνίτης
names.note: Skammonia root = scammony; standard identification.

names.name: σκαμμωνία
names.note: Source of scammony resin; Berendes: Convolvulus scammonia; uncontroversial.

names.name: κόριον
names.note: Korion; uncontroversial.

names.name: σύμφυτον πετραῖον
names.note: Woody fragrant rock plant, origanum-like branches, thyme-like heads, reddish root; uncertain.

names.name: οὖα
names.note: Oua (sorbs) dried for diarrhoea; standard.

names.name: κρανία
names.note: Olive-like oblong fruit turning yellow/waxy, edible, astringent; standard.

names.name: ἡ δύσαρον τὸ ὑπὸ τῶν μυρεψῶν καλούμενον πελεκῖνος
names.note: Hedysaron/pelekinos with axe-like seed; Berendes Coronilla securidaca (syn. Securigera securidaca).

names.name: Hazel-Nut
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: The Sea Coleworts
names.note: Thick wrinkled greyish leaves, white four-petalled flowers, Kent and Essex coasts fit sea kale.

names.name: μέσπιλον
names.note: Thorny aronia with small three-stoned apple-like fruit = azarole; Italian second kind (setanion) = medlar.

names.name: ἀνθυλλίς
names.note: First anthyllis lentil-leaved, salty = Cressa cretica (Berendes); second ajuga-like kind uncertain.

names.name: κρῆθμον
names.note: Seashore rock plant with fleshy salty leaves, pickled; standard.

names.name: Samphire
names.note: Rock samphire explicitly described.

names.name: κρόκος
names.note: Corycian saffron stigmas; standard identification.

names.name: κροκόμαγμα
names.note: Pressed residue of saffron unguent (multi-ingredient); mapped to eponymous saffron.

names.name: κρόκινον
names.note: Oil perfumed with saffron.

names.name: Saffron
names.note: Saffron.

names.name: κραταιόγονον
names.note: Wheat-like leaves, millet-like seed; Fraas Crucianella monspeliaca, Sprengel Polygonum persicaria.

names.name: Crosswort
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: σίκυς ἥμερος
names.note: Janick & Paris 2007: classical sikys mostly snake/chate melon (traditionally cucumber); pepon (melon) also treated.

names.name: Cucumbers
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κύμινον τὸ ἥμερον
names.note: Cultivated kyminon (Ethiopian 'royal' cumin); Berendes Cuminum cyminum.

names.name: κυπάρισσος
names.note: Standard identification; leaves and green cones ('sphairia') used.

names.name: κύπερος Ἰνδικός
names.note: Indian 'cyperus' like ginger, saffron-yellow and bitter when chewed: turmeric (Berendes, Beck).

names.name: κυκλάμινος
names.note: Ivy-like variegated leaves, round tuber; Cyclamen certain, species uncertain.

names.name: σχοῖνος
names.note: Aromatic rush from Libya/Arabia/Nabataea used in unguents; camel grass per Berendes/Beck.

names.name: Artichokes
names.note: Garden artichoke (Cynara scolymus = C. cardunculus); standard identification.

names.name: ἄγρωστις
names.note: Creeping jointed grass with sweet jointed roots, cattle fodder; Bermuda or couch grass.

names.name: Hound’S Tongue
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: πάπυρος
names.note: Plant from which paper (chartes) is made; standard.

names.name: κύπερος
names.note: Leek-like leaves, triangular stem, black fragrant olive-like tubers; C. rotundus or C. longus per Berendes/Beck.

names.name: Broom, And Broom-Rape
names.note: Broom; broom-rape parasitic on it = Orobanche rapum-genistae.

names.name: ἔβενος
names.note: Best ebony Ethiopian (African blackwood); Indian kind with streaks is Diospyros ebony.

names.name: χαμαιδάφνη
names.note: Sprengel/Berendes: Ruscus racemosus (= Danae racemosa); smooth laurel-like leaves, red round fruit.

names.name: ἔλαιον διὰ κνιδίου κόκκου
names.note: Cnidian berry (kokkos knidios) is the fruit of Daphne gnidium (standard).

names.name: θυμελαίτης
names.note: Thymelaia = Daphne gnidium; standard identification.

names.name: θυμελαία
names.note: Source of Cnidian berries, flax-like shrub; Berendes: Südlicher Seidelbast.

names.name: δαφνοειδές
names.note: Laurel-like acrid leaves, black fruit; Renaissance Laureola; Berendes: Daphne alpina.

names.name: χαμελαία
names.note: Berendes: Daphne oleoides; olive-like bitter leaves; traditional pre-Linnaean Chamelaea is Cneorum tricoccon.

names.name: RV: δελφίνιον
names.note: RV-text chapter; dolphin-shaped flowers; Sibthorp D. ajacis, Fraas D. peregrinum; second kind D. tenuissimum.

names.name: Flux-Weed
names.note: Flux-weed (Sophia chirurgorum); standard identification.

names.name: Clove Gilliflowers
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Fox-Glove
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἄμπελος ἀγρία
names.note: Berendes: Tamus communis (= Dioscorea communis); clustered berries red when ripe.

names.name: Black Cresses
names.note: Speculative: yellow-flowered crucifer with deeply cut leaves on walls and rubbish around London; not otherwise identifiable.

names.name: Rocket
names.note: Wild rocket with finely cut leaves, yellow flowers, long pods; garden rocket omitted.

names.name: δίψακος
names.note: Leaf-cups collecting water; Berendes Dipsacus silvestris (= D. fullonum).

names.name: The Fuller’S Thistle, Or Teasle
names.note: Clothworkers' teasel with hooked bracts; wild teasel also described.

names.name: κόνυζα
names.note: Greater konyza; Berendes Erigeron viscosum; small kind E. graveolens; third Inula britannica.

names.name: οἶνος κονυζίτης ὁμοίως σκευάζεται
names.note: Konyza; larger kind usually Dittrichia (Inula) viscosa, smaller D. graveolens.

names.name: κόστος
names.note: Arabian, Indian and Syrian costus: aromatic root of costus (standard; syn. Saussurea costus, S. lappa).

names.name: ἀκόνιτον
names.note: Pardalianches with cyclamen-like leaves and scorpion-tail root; Doronicum (Berendes).

names.name: Nailwort, Or Whitlow-Grass
names.note: Tiny annual with small white flowers: whitlow grass.

names.name: κιννάβαρι οἴονταί τινες τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπάρχειν τῷ καλουμένῳ μινίῳ πλανώμενοι
names.note: Distinguished from Spanish minium (true cinnabar); costly Libyan kinnabari 'thought dragon's blood', often read as Dracaena resin; debated.

names.name: δρακόντιον
names.note: Snake-like purple-spotted stem fits dragon arum; Berendes assigns this description to Arum italicum.

names.name: Dragons
names.note: Garden 'dragons' with snake-like mottled stalks; standard identification.

names.name: τὸ δὲ σκιλλητικὸν
names.note: Vinegar of white skilla (sea squill); standard identification.

names.name: ὁ δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς σκίλλης ρἶνος γίνεται οὕτω
names.note: Wine of dried sea squill (skilla).

names.name: σκίλλα
names.note: Squill; standard identification (Urginea maritima = Drimia maritima).

names.name: Rosa Solis, Or Sun Dew
names.note: Round leaves with red glandular hairs, moist in heat: sundew.

names.name: βότρυς
names.note: Botrys, yellowish fragrant herb; Berendes Chenopodium botrys.

names.name: σίκυς ἄγριος
names.note: Wild cucumber yielding elaterium; Berendes: Ecballium elaterium; uncontroversial.

names.name: πάνακες Ἀσκληπίον
names.note: Fennel-like rough leaves, golden umbels; Berendes Echinophora tenuifolia.

names.name: ἔχιον
names.note: Rough narrow leaves, seed like a viper's head; Echium certain, species uncertain.

names.name: Viper’S Bugloss
names.note: Rough prickly stalks; viper's bugloss.

names.name: καρδάμωμον
names.note: Traditional identification as cardamom; stated origins (Commagene, Armenia) make the ancient source debated.

names.name: Dog’S-Grass, Or Cough Grass
names.note: Dog's-grass/couch grass; standard identification.

names.name: τράγος
names.note: Leafless seaside shrublet with red berry-like clusters; Ephedra.

names.name: ἐπιμήδιον
names.note: Ivy-like leaves, said flowerless, antifertility root; Epimedium named from it, identification uncertain.

names.name: ἵππουρις
names.note: Hollow jointed stems with whorls, wet places; horsetail.

names.name: ἔστι δὲ καὶ
names.note: Second hippouris with shorter, whiter, softer 'hair'; another horsetail.

names.name: Horsetail
names.note: 'Great horsetail' with asparagus-like fertile shoots; many kinds treated together.

names.name: ἐρείκη
names.note: Bushy tamarisk-like shrub visited by bees for poor honey; heath (tree heath standard).

names.name: εὔζωμον
names.note: Aphrodisiac salad herb and seed; standard.

names.name: ἡρύγγη
names.note: Spiny plant with edible young leaves; standard E. campestre.

names.name: Eringo, Or Sea-Holly
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: τιθύμαλλος
names.note: Seven kinds of tithymallos (charakias, myrsinites, paralios etc.); all Euphorbia.

names.name: ἄπιος
names.note: Pear-shaped tuber, purgative; Berendes: Birnwolfsmilch; name preserved in E. apios.

names.name: χαμαισύκη
names.note: Milky prostrate branches with lentil-like leaves; Berendes: Erdfeige.

names.name: λαθυρίς
names.note: Counted among tithymalloi; hollow stem, capsules; name preserved in E. lathyris.

names.name: πεπλίς
names.note: Seaside milky prostrate herb ('wild purslane'); standard identification.

names.name: πέπλος
names.note: Small milky shrublet; Berendes: Peplos; standard identification.

names.name: πιτύουσα
names.note: Pine-like leaved spurge; Berendes: Pityusa; name preserved in Euphorbia pithyusa.

names.name: εὐφόρβιον
names.note: Ferula-like tree of Mauretanian Atlas, acrid latex (Juba's euphorbium).

names.name: ἱπποφαές
names.note: Fullers' spiny seaside shrub with purgative sap; Berendes: Euphorbia spinosa; not modern Hippophae.

names.name: Eyebright
names.note: Common eyebright (aggregate); standard identification.

names.name: The Beech Tree
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: σίλφιον
names.note: Cyrenaic silphium unidentified (extinct?); Median/Syrian kinds are asafoetida-type Ferula.

names.name: νάρθηκος χλωροῦ ἡ
names.note: Narthex pith; uncontroversial.

names.name: μετώπιον
names.note: Egyptian multi-ingredient unguent named for galbanum (metopion tree); mapped to galbanum source.

names.name: χαλβάνη
names.note: Gum-resin of a Syrian narthex; Berendes Ferula galbaniflua/rubricaulis (= F. gummosa).

names.name: ἀμμωνιακόν
names.note: Gum of a Cyrenaican ferula; Berendes F. tingitana; Persian trade ammoniac from Dorema ammoniacum (= Ferula ammoniacum).

names.name: σαγαπηνόν
names.note: Gum of a ferula-like Median plant; Berendes probable source Ferula persica or F. szowitsiana.

names.name: ἄλυσσον
names.note: Double shield-like silicles; Sprengel/Fraas Farsetia clypeata (= Fibigia clypeata).

names.name: χελιδόνιον μικρόν
names.note: Stemless small herb with tuberous roots; Ranunculus ficaria = Ficaria verna.

names.name: The Lesser Celandine, Usually Known By The Name Of Pilewort And Fogwort
names.note: Pilewort; standard identification.

names.name: σκευάζεται καὶ ὁ
names.note: Wine from sykomora (sycamore fig).

names.name: συκόμορον
names.note: Large fig-like tree with mulberry-like leaves, fruit scraped to ripen; standard.

names.name: κῆμος
names.note: Tiny woolly herb with fruit hidden in downy heads; cudweed proposed.

names.name: Cudweed, Or Cottonweed
names.note: Common cudweed of dry sandy ground with brownish-yellow flowers among narrow woolly leaves; several cudweeds included.

names.name: Queen Of The Meadows, Meadow Sweet, Or Mead Sweet
names.note: Reddish stalks, elm-like pinnate leaves: meadowsweet.

names.name: ἀγαρικόν
names.note: Spongy silphium-like 'root'; standard identification larch polypore (Berendes: Lärchenschwamm).

names.name: Strawberries
names.note: Strawberries.

names.name: The Black Alder-Tree
names.note: Black alder of herbals = alder buckthorn with purgative bark; standard identification.

names.name: ἔμπετρον
names.note: Salty-tasting herb of coastal rocks; Fraas: Frankenia pulverulenta, Brunfels/Sprengel: Crithmum.

names.name: Ash Tree
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: μελία
names.note: Melia is ash; Greek species most likely manna ash or narrow-leaved ash.

names.name: χρυσοκόμη οἱ δὲ
names.note: Span-high stem with golden hyssop-like corymb; Chrysocoma/Linosyris traditional.

names.name: γεντιανή
names.note: Named after Illyrian king Gentius; Berendes Enzian; standard G. lutea.

names.name: Gentian, Felwort, Or Baldmony
names.note: English felwort (purple, Kent chalk) fits Gentianella; imported gentian root is Gentiana lutea.

names.name: Dove’S-Foot, Or Crane’S-Bill
names.note: Small cranesbill with very small red flowers; dove's-foot usually G. molle.

names.name: Herb Robert
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: γεράνιον
names.note: Round sweet edible root; Berendes Geranium tuberosum; second kind Erodium malacoides.

names.name: Avens, Called Also Colewort, And Herb Bonet
names.note: Avens / herb bennet; standard identification.

names.name: ξιφίον
names.note: Sword-shaped iris-like leaves, cornfield plant; Mediterranean gladiolus.

names.name: γλαύκιον
names.note: Juice of Syrian plant with horned-poppy leaves; Berendes 'ohne Zweifel' Glaucium corniculatum.

names.name: μήκων κερατῖτις
names.note: Horned seaside poppy with white hairy leaves; yellow horned poppy.

names.name: βούφθαλμον
names.note: Fennel-like leaves, large yellow 'ox-eye' flowers; Berendes Chrysanthemum coronarium.

names.name: Alehoof, Or Ground-Ivy
names.note: Alehoof = ground-ivy; standard identification.

names.name: ἄλυπον
names.note: Reddish shrubby coastal plant with purgative seed; Berendes: Globularia alypum.

names.name: Hedge Hyssop
names.note: Italian garden kind = Gratiola; described wild English sorts (purple, spotted, bogs) fit Scutellaria minor.

names.name: δρυοπτερίς
names.note: Small fern on mossy old oaks; most authors Polypodium dryopteris; Fraas Asplenium adiantum-nigrum (Berendes).

names.name: βάκχαρις
names.note: Berendes: undetermined; Fraas Gnaphalium sanguineum; cinnamon-scented root.

names.name: ἑλίχρυσον ἢ χρυσάνθεμον
names.note: Golden everlasting used to crown images; Helichrysum.

names.name: ἡλιοτρόπιον τὸ μικρόν
names.note: Marsh and lake-side herb with hanging wart-like fruit; Fraas: H. supinum; older: Croton tinctorium.

names.name: Black Hellebore
names.note: Christmas-herb/flowers = H. niger; bear's-foot and setterwort names also cover H. foetidus, H. viridis.

names.name: ἐλλεβορίτης
names.note: Black helleboros; Greek plant usually H. cyclophyllus, now H. odorus subsp. cyclophyllus; formerly read H. niger.

names.name: ἐλλέβορος μέλας
names.note: Berendes after Boissier: Greek H. cyclophyllus (now H. odorus subsp. cyclophyllus); older view H. orientalis.

names.name: ἡμεροκαλλές
names.note: Lily-like, leek-green leaves, yellow flowers; Berendes: not determined; Hemerocallis fulva or Lilium bulbiferum.

names.name: Rupture-Wort
names.note: Prostrate thready branches, tiny yellowish flowers: rupturewort.

names.name: Hawk-Weed
names.note: Several sorts; runcinate basal leaves and rough branched stalk fit Crepis or Picris as well as Hieracium.

names.name: πολύγονον θῆλυ
names.note: Single reed-like stem, trumpet-like joints, pine-like whorls, by water; Hippuris or Equisetum proposed.

names.name: μάκιρ
names.note: Thick yellowish astringent bark from 'barbarian' lands, for dysentery; identity uncertain (kurchi bark proposed; medieval confusion with mace).

names.name: Hops
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὑάκινθος
names.note: Bulbous plant with span-high stem and bent purple-flowered head; classical hyacinth disputed.

names.name: Orpine
names.note: Fleshy leaves, tufted flowers, tuberous roots: orpine.

names.name: ὑοσκύαμος
names.note: Three henbanes by flower colour; the preferred white kind is H. albus.

names.name: ὑοσκυάμινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil from white henbane seed; white seed indicates Hyoscyamus albus.

names.name: Henbane
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὑπήκοον
names.note: Grain-field weed with rue-like leaves, poppy-like juice; Hypecoum.

names.name: ἄσκυρον
names.note: Larger hypericum, yellow flowers, fruit staining fingers blood-red; species uncertain.

names.name: ἀνδρόσαιμον
names.note: Shrubby hypericum with wine-red juice and resinous smell; species debated.

names.name: Tustan, Or Park Leaves
names.note: Tutsan, park leaves.

names.name: κόρις
names.note: Heath-like red leaves, called hypericum; H. coris named from it, H. empetrifolium fits Greece.

names.name: πάνακες Χειρώνιον
names.note: Pelion plant, marjoram-like leaves, golden flower; Fraas Hypericum olympicum; others Inula, Helianthemum.

names.name: St. John’S Wort
names.note: Common St John's wort; pellucid-dotted opposite leaves, yellow star flowers.

names.name: St. Peter’S Wort
names.note: Square stalks, larger and with few dots, damp places; Ascyron of herbals.

names.name: ὑπερικόν
names.note: Rue-like leaves, resin-scented black seed; Berendes H. crispum (=triquetrifolium); H. perforatum also proposed.

names.name: Holly, Holm, Or Hulver Bush
names.note: Holly/hulver is the standard English name for Ilex aquifolium; Culpeper gives no description.

names.name: Masterwort
names.note: Common masterwort with ternate leaves; GBIF-accepted name, syn. Peucedanum ostruthium.

names.name: τοῦ δὲ λεγομένου
names.note: Indikon: 'foam of Indian reeds' = indigo; second kind is dyers' scum from vats.

names.name: The Yellow Water-Flag, Or Flower-De-Luce
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἰσόπυρον
names.note: Tendril-tipped leaf, anise-like leaves, seeds tasting like nigella; uncertain.

names.name: Ragwort
names.note: St James-wort/staggerwort with torn leaves: common ragwort.

names.name: Rushes
names.note: Bulrushes and soft rushes collectively; no description.

names.name: σχοίνου ἑλείας τὸ
names.note: Oxyschoinos and holoschoinos marsh rushes; sharp rush and round-headed club-rush.

names.name: Juniper Bush
names.note: Common juniper bush; berries used medicinally.

common_name: cedar, juniper, cypress, laurel, pine and fir wood wines

names.name: ὁ δὲ κέδρινος
names.note: Several wood wines; first kedros (prickly juniper); arkeuthos, kyparissos, daphne, pitys, elate.

names.name: ἄρκευθος
names.note: Large and small arkeuthos; berries hazelnut- to bean-sized. Prickly juniper usual; large kind possibly J. drupacea.

names.name: ἐλατίνη
names.note: Like helxine but smaller, rounder, hairy leaves; fluellen (Linaria elatine).

names.name: Fluellin, Or Lluellin
names.note: First sort with roundish leaves; second with eared leaves = sharp-leaved fluellen (K. elatine).

names.name: Scabious, Three Sorts
names.note: Common field scabious with pale blue heads; smaller sort likely S. columbaria.

names.name: κολόκυνθα ἐδώδιμος
names.note: Edible kolokynthe of antiquity is the bottle gourd (Cucurbita is American).

names.name: κύμινον ἄγριον
names.note: Small plant with 5-6 round heads; Sprengel and Fraas Lagoecia cuminoides.

names.name: Archangel
names.note: Archangel = dead-nettles; white, red and yellow kinds (yellow = L. galeobdolon).

names.name: λευκάς
names.note: Fragmentary chapter; Berendes only conjectures: Sprengel Lamium maculatum, Fraas Lamium striatum.

names.name: ἀστράγαλος
names.note: Chickpea-like leaves, small purple flowers, horn-like intertwined roots (Pheneos); Orobus/Lathyrus proposed.

names.name: κλύμενον
names.note: Square bean-like stem, plantain-like leaves, pods curling like octopus arms; Lathyrus or Scorpiurus proposed.

names.name: Lavender
names.note: Garden lavender of English gardens.

names.name: στοιχάς
names.note: From the Stoechades islands off Marseille; Berendes L. stoechas.

names.name: σκευάζεται καὶ ὁ
names.note: Stoichas = French lavender; standard identification.

names.name: γίνεται καὶ ὄξος
names.note: Vinegar steeped with stoichas herb.

names.name: κύπρινον
names.note: Oil of kypros flowers (henna), standard identification.

names.name: κύπρος
names.note: Olive-like leaves, white fragrant clustered flowers, best from Ascalon and Canopus: henna (standard).

names.name: λεοντοπέταλον
names.note: Sprengel Leontice leontopetalum; Fraas Roemeria hybrida (pods, red flower) — debated.

names.name: Motherwort
names.note: Square stalk, lobed leaves, whorled flowers: motherwort.

names.name: Mithridate Mustard
names.note: Taller biennial, smaller round pouches, sharper taste; names applied to both species.

names.name: Buck’S Horn
names.note: Swine-cresses; trailing, small jagged leaves, whitish clustered flowers on dry ground fit swine-cress.

names.name: δράβη
names.note: Berendes: Lepidium draba (Türkische Kresse); Cappadocian seed used as pepper substitute.

names.name: Sciatica Cresses
names.note: Speculative: herbalists' Iberis/sciatica cress; two white-flowered wayside crucifers with sharp seed.

names.name: κάρδαμον
names.note: Pungent seed, best from Babylon; standard identification as garden cress.

names.name: Privet
names.note: Common privet for arbours and topiary.

names.name: λειμώνιον
names.note: Beet-like leaves, lily-like stem with red astringent fruit, meadows and marshes; Limonium traditional, uncertain.

names.name: Flax-Weed, Or Toad-Flax
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: καὶ τὸ λινόσπεπμον
names.note: Linosperm (flax seed), same virtues as fenugreek; uncontroversial.

names.name: Lungwort
names.note: Broad greyish leafy 'moss' on oaks and beeches without flowers: the lichen Lobaria pulmonaria.

names.name: φοῖνιξ
names.note: Barley-like leaves, darnel-like spike, in fields and on new roofs; ryegrass or wall barley proposed.

names.name: κυκλάμινος ἑτέρα
names.note: Kissanthemon: twining, white fragrant flowers, berries; Berendes: Lonicera periclymenum.

names.name: περικλύμενον
names.note: Twining shrub with perfoliate leaves bearing berries; honeysuckle, Greek species likely.

names.name: Woodbine, Or Honey-Suckles
names.note: Woodbine/honeysuckle.

names.name: ἄκανθα λευκή
names.note: Sea-urchin-like spiny head, purple flowers; Berendes Cnicus ferox (= Cirsium/Lophiolepis ferox), others Cnicus acarna; uncertain.

names.name: θέρμος
names.note: Cultivated lupin; smaller wild lupin also mentioned.

names.name: ῥάμνος
names.note: Thorny hedge shrub with oblong soft fleshy leaves, three kinds; Lycium europaeum or Rhamnus spp. proposed.

names.name: λυκαψός
names.note: Lykapsos, long rough lettuce-like leaves; field bugloss Lycopsis (Anchusa) arvensis, traditional.

names.name: Moneywort, Or Herb Twopence
names.note: Creeping stems with paired round leaves: moneywort/herb twopence.

names.name: Loosestrife, With Spiked Heads Of Flowers
names.note: Square stalks, long spikes of flowers; purple loosestrife.

names.name: One-Blade
names.note: One-blade (Unifolium) of the herbalists; standard identification.

names.name: One Blade
names.note: One/two ribbed leaves, white star flowers: one-blade.

names.name: μηλέα
names.note: Apple trees generally, especially quince; also Persian (peach), Armenian (apricot) and Median apples (citron).

names.name: ἀλκαίας
names.note: Wild mallow with leaves cut like hiera botane; Berendes/Beck Malva alcea.

names.name: μανδραγόρας
names.note: Male and female mandrake; female often called M. autumnalis, which GBIF sinks into M. officinarum.

names.name: μανδραγορίτης
names.note: Root bark of mandragoras; Mediterranean mandrake.

names.name: ἀνθεμίς
names.note: Three kinds by ray colour: white = chamomile, yellow = Anthemis tinctoria, purple = Anthemis rosea (Berendes).

names.name: Heart Trefoil
names.note: Leaf with heart-shaped flesh-coloured spot fits spotted medick.

names.name: κύτισος
names.note: White shrub with fenugreek/trefoil-like leaves; tree medick (Berendes).

names.name: Μηδική
names.note: 'Median herb'; trefoil-like fodder with twisted pods; Berendes: Medicago sativa.

names.name: μελίλωτος
names.note: Saffron-coloured fragrant Attic kind; Berendes Melilotus creticus, M. neapolitanus; Sprengel M. officinalis.

names.name: Mellilot, Or King’S Claver
names.note: Yellow scented trefoil flowers: melilot/King's claver.

names.name: σισύμβριον οἱ δὲ ἕρπυλλον ἄγριον μέγαν καλοῦσιν
names.note: Mint-like, broader-leaved, fragrant; usual identification water mint (Berendes 'Wasserminze').

names.name: φύλλον
names.note: Rock plant with thelygonon/arrhenogonon forms; Fraas Mercurialis perennis; Sprengel M. tomentosa.

names.name: Dog Mercury
names.note: Dog mercury, unbranched stalks, woodland.

names.name: The Medlar
names.note: Medlar tree described; five-petalled white flowers.

names.name: περσαία
names.note: Egyptian tree with edible fruit, esp. Thebaid: Egyptian persea (Mimusops), not avocado; poison legend.

names.name: ἀντίρρινον
names.note: Wild lychnis-like plant, seed pod like a calf's snout; snapdragon.

names.name: βαλάνινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil of balanos myrepsike (ben nut), generally Moringa peregrina.

names.name: βάλανος μυρεψική
names.note: Perfumers' nut pressed for oil, tree like tamarisk; Berendes: Salbeneichel (Moringa).

names.name: βολβὸς ἐδώδιμος
names.note: Berendes: Muscari comosum (Schopfhyacinthe), the bitter edible bulb still eaten in the Mediterranean.

names.name: βολβὸς ἐμετικός
names.note: Berendes: Muscari moschatum (= Muscarimia muscari) or Narcissus jonquilla; bulb with black tunic, emetic.

names.name: μυὸς ὦτα
names.note: Paired narrow leaves, small bluish flowers; Sprengel Myosotis palustris, Fraas Asperugo procumbens.

names.name: μυριόφυλλον
names.note: Single tender stem, fennel-like leaves, marshes; water milfoil.

names.name: μυρσίνινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil from tender leaves of black myrtle.

names.name: μυρτίτην δὲ δεῖ
names.note: Juice of ripe black myrtle berries (myrta).

names.name: μυρσινίης δὲ σκευάζεται οὕτω
names.note: Branches, leaves and berries of black myrtle (myrsine).

names.name: μυρσίνη
names.note: Cultivated myrtle, black and white kinds; standard.

names.name: ναρκίσσινον
names.note: Oil perfumed with narcissus flowers; species uncertain.

names.name: νάρκισσος
names.note: Berendes: Narcissus poeticus or N. tazetta; leek-like leaves, bulb.

names.name: νάρδος Ἰνδική καὶ Συριακή
names.note: Indian and 'Syrian' nard are both spikenard rhizomes traded via different routes (Berendes, Beck).

names.name: νάρδινον μύρον
names.note: Multi-ingredient unguent named after spikenard.

names.name: κύαμος Αἰγύπτιος
names.note: Pond plant with hat-like leaf, rose flower, wasp-nest seed head (kiborion), root kolokasion; standard.

names.name: Bifoil Or Twablade
names.note: Bifoil/twayblade orchid with paired leaves; standard identification.

names.name: Nep, Or Catmint
names.note: Garden nep/catmint, hoary square stalks.

names.name: ν ήριον
names.note: Rhododendron/rhododaphne with almond-like leaves; oleander.

names.name: English Tobacco
names.note: English tobacco, smaller than the Indian kind.

names.name: ἐστι δὲ καὶ ἕτερον γένος ἀγρίου κυμίνου
names.note: Horn-like capsules with nigella-like seed; Sprengel N. arvensis, Fraas N. aristata (= N. arvensis subsp. aristata).

names.name: μελάνθιον
names.note: Melanthion; uncontroversial.

names.name: νυμφαία
names.note: White water lily; second nymphaia with yellow flower = Nuphar lutea (Berendes).

names.name: Water Lily
names.note: Covers white and yellow water lilies; main white kind Nymphaea alba, yellow Nuphar lutea.

names.name: λωτὸς ὁ ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ γεννώμενος ἐν τῷ ὕδατι τῶν πεδίων ἐπικλυσθέντων
names.note: Egyptian water lotus of flooded plains, poppy-like seed head; Nymphaea lotus.

names.name: ἔλαιον
names.note: Olive oil, especially omphacinum from unripe olives.

names.name: ἐλαιόμελι
names.note: Sweet thick exudate from olive trunks at Palmyra per Dioscorides; nature of the product uncertain.

names.name: ἀμόργη
names.note: Watery dregs of pressed olives boiled down.

names.name: ἀγριελαία
names.note: Wild olive (kotinos, var. sylvestris), with olive oils and 'Ethiopian olive' tear.

names.name: ῤνοβρυχίς
names.note: Lentil-like leaves, purple flower, moist untilled ground; genus named from it, species uncertain.

names.name: Cock’S Head, Red Fitching, Or Medick Fetch
names.note: Cock's head/medick fetch with pale reddish spikes and rough flat pods; standard identification.

names.name: ἄκανθα Ἀραβική
names.note: Berendes: not determined; Sprengel tentatively Onopordon arabicum; only virtues given.

names.name: ἄγχουσα ἑτέρα
names.note: Smaller rough-leaved anchusa, purple-red flowers, red roots, sandy places; borage family, species uncertain.

names.name: ὄνοσμα
names.note: Anchusa-like leaves; Fraas Onosma echioides; Sprengel wavered (Lithospermum/Anchusa).

names.name: Adder’S Tongue Or Serpent’S Tongue
names.note: Single leaf with tongue-like spike; standard identification.

names.name: πανακίτης
names.note: Panax (Herakleion) source of opopanax; usually Opopanax hispidus/chironium.

names.name: Orchis
names.note: Tuberous orchids collectively (dog-stones, satyrion); only roots described.

names.name: σατύριον
names.note: Three-leaved bulbous aphrodisiac; Fraas Aceras anthropophora, Sprengel Tulipa; erythronion part also undetermined.

names.name: ὄρχις ἕτερος
names.note: Leek-like leaves, purple flowers; Sprengel declined, Fraas Orchis undulatifolia (= O. italica).

names.name: δίκταμνον
names.note: Cretan herb like pennyroyal; chapter adds pseudodiktamnon.

names.name: δικταμνίτης
names.note: Diktamnon = Cretan dittany; standard identification.

names.name: ἡ δὲ ὀνῖτις
names.note: Whiter, more hyssop-like leaves; usual O. onites; Berendes 'Origanum creticum'.

names.name: μᾶρον ἢ ὑσόβρυον
names.note: Berendes: not certain; Teucrium marum abandoned, Sibthorp/Fraas Origanum sipyleum (Magnesia, Tralles).

names.name: ὔσσωπος
names.note: Not described; Sprengel/Fraas Origanum syriacum/smyrnaeum, Lenz Hyssopus officinalis (rare in Greece).

names.name: ὀρνιθόγαλον
names.note: Berendes: Ornithogalum umbellatum; milk-white flowers, edible bulb; species within genus debated.

names.name: Bird’S Foot
names.note: Small heath legume with jointed claw-like pods; larger whitish-red second sort uncertain.

names.name: ὀροβάγχη
names.note: Leafless reddish parasitic stem choking pulses, eaten like asparagus: broomrape (O. crenata on legumes).

names.name: ὄρυζα τῶν σιτηρῶν
names.note: Cereal of marshy places; rice, uncontroversial.

names.name: Osmond Royal, Or Water Fern
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὄσυρις
names.note: Dark slender shrublet with flax-like leaves; Berendes: Osyris alba.

names.name: Wood Sorrel
names.note: Trefoil leaves notched at the ends: wood sorrel.

names.name: παλίουρος
names.note: Well-known spiny shrub with oily seed; standard identification.

names.name: παγκράτιον
names.note: Berendes: Pancratium maritimum; large reddish bitter bulb, lily-like leaves, squill-like action.

names.name: κέγχρος ἀτροφωτέρα τῶν
names.note: Kenchros = common millet; standard identification.

names.name: μήκων ῥοιάς
names.note: Rhoeas, quickly sheds its petals, in fields; corn poppy.

names.name: Pellitory Of The Wall
names.note: Reddish brittle stems on walls; British species is P. judaica, older texts say P. officinalis.

names.name: ἑλξίνη
names.note: Parthenion/helxine; pellitory; Greek plant likely P. judaica.

names.name: Herb True-Love, Or One-Berry
names.note: Herb true-love/one-berry; standard identification.

names.name: ἡ δὲ ἐν τῷ Παρνασσῷ ἄγρωστις γεννωμένη πολυκλαδωτέρα ἐστί
names.note: Parnassian 'agrostis' with ivy-like leaves, white fragrant flower; Linnaean Parnassia named from it, uncertain.

names.name: παρωνυχία
names.note: Small rock plant like peplos, cures whitlows; Paronychia or Draba proposed.

names.name: καλοῦσί τινες πήγανον
names.note: 'Wild rue' called moly in Cappadocia and Galatia; standard Peganum harmala.

names.name: φαληρίς
names.note: Zea-like stems, white millet-sized seed; Berendes Phalaris nodosa (= P. aquatica), Sprengel P. canariensis.

names.name: French Beans
names.note: Kidney/French bean; standard identification.

names.name: φιλύρα
names.note: Olive-like broader darker leaves, black sweetish clustered fruit; not lime-tree: Phillyrea (Berendes).

names.name: ἐλάτινον
names.note: Elate here likely the date-palm spathe (cf. Diosc. 1.109, astringent like rose oil); fir less likely.

names.name: φοινικίτης
names.note: Wine of ripe dates (phoinikes).

names.name: φοῖνιξ
names.note: Egyptian dates (phoinikobalanoi, karyotides); standard.

names.name: κάλαμος
names.note: Several reeds listed; medicinal root is of phragmites (common reed); donax/Cyprian reed = giant cane.

names.name: Mouse-Ear
names.note: Stoloniferous hairy rosette, milky sap, single pale yellow head.

names.name: ἄνσσον
names.note: Anison; uncontroversial.

names.name: Burnet Saxifrage
names.note: Burnet saxifrage with white umbels; greater sort is P. major.

names.name: ὁ δὲ ῥητινίτης κατὰ τὰ ἔθνη σκευάζεται ποικίλως
names.note: Wine with peuke (pine) resin, Galatia; pine species uncertain.

names.name: ο ἶνος πισσίτης σκευάζεται διὰ πίσσης ὑγρᾶς καὶ γλεύκους
names.note: Liquid pitch (pissa hygra) from pines in must; species unspecified.

names.name: πίσσα
names.note: Liquid and dry pitch drawn from the resinous wood of peuke and pitys (pines).

names.name: πίτυς
names.note: Pitys and the related peuke (pines); pitys usually Aleppo pine, peuke black pine; strobilos = stone pine. Genus Pinus certain.

names.name: στροβιλίτης δὲ σκευάζεται
names.note: Fresh crushed strobiloi (pine cones) in must; strobilos usually stone pine.

names.name: πέπερι
names.note: Indian pepper tree; long, white and black pepper treated together; long pepper is Piper longum.

names.name: σχίνινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil from ripe fruit of schinos (lentisk).

names.name: μαστίχινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil made from mastic resin of lentisk.

names.name: καὶ ὁ σχίνινος δὲ ἐοικότως τῷ μυρσινίτῃ σκευάζεται
names.note: Schinos (lentisk) wine; terebinth (terminthos) wine made likewise.

names.name: σχῖνος
names.note: Astringent shrub whose resin (schinine, mastiche) is best from Chios: mastic tree (standard).

names.name: τέρμινθος
