names.note: Terebinth tree with edible fruit and resin; standard identification.

names.name: πιστάκια
names.note: Syrian pistachios; standard.

names.name: στρατιώτης ὁ ἐπὶ τῶν ὑδάτων φυόμενος
names.note: Rootless floating plant with aeizoon-like leaves; water lettuce.

names.name: ὁλόστεον
names.note: Tiny herb with coronopus-like leaves and hair-thin root; Plantago proposed; Holosteum shares the name only.

names.name: πλάτανος
names.note: Plane tree native to Greece; standard identification.

names.name: πολύγαλον
names.note: Span-high, lentil-like leaves, galactagogue; Berendes: Polygala venulosa.

names.name: Solomon’S Seal
names.note: Arching stalk with alternate leaves like lily of the valley.

names.name: πολυγόνατον
names.note: Mountain plant with bay-like leaves; Solomon's seal (named from it).

names.name: λογχῖτις ἑτέρα τραχεῖα
names.note: Fern like scolopendrion but rougher and more divided; holly fern traditional, uncertain.

names.name: Golden Maiden Hair
names.note: Hair-like leaves and golden capsule in a husk, in bogs/heaths: haircap moss.

names.name: αἴγειρος
names.note: Aigeiros = black poplar; resin and Eridanus amber legend mentioned.

names.name: Water-Caltrops
names.note: Names belong to Trapa natans, said absent; the two described English kinds are pondweeds (Potamogeton).

names.name: ποταμογείτων
names.note: Beet-like leaf rising a little above water; pondweed.

names.name: Tormentil, Or Septfoil
names.note: Like cinquefoil but with stalkless leaves: tormentil/septfoil.

names.name: Burnet
names.note: Garden burnet = salad burnet (Sanguisorba minor); the described great wild burnet = Sanguisorba officinalis.

names.name: Cowslips, Or Peagles
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Primroses
names.note: Primroses.

names.name: Self-Heal
names.note: Self-heal, prunel, carpenter's herb.

names.name: ἀμυγδάλη
names.note: Bitter and sweet almonds; standard.

names.name: ἀμυγδάλινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil of bitter almonds (metopion); syn. Prunus dulcis.

names.name: The Peach Tree
names.note: Peach tree described.

names.name: The Black Thorn, Or Sloe-Bush
names.note: Blackthorn/sloe.

names.name: θηλυπτερίς
names.note: Many fronds, not from one stock; Berendes: Pteris aquilina (bracken).

names.name: ῥοίτης δὲ οἶνος σκευάζεται οὕτως
names.note: Juice of seedless pomegranates (rhoa).

names.name: ῥόα
names.note: Pomegranate fruit, rind (sidia), flowers (kytinoi), roots; standard.

names.name: βαλαύστιον
names.note: Flower of wild pomegranate; standard.

names.name: Winter-Green
names.note: Pear-like leaves, open star-like fragrant white flowers, northern woods; Pyrola.

names.name: δρῦς
names.note: All oaks (drys, phegos, prinos); Sardian acorns (kastaneia) are chestnuts.

names.name: κηκίς
names.note: Oak galls; best omphakitis (small, knobby, unperforated) = Aleppo galls of Q. infectoria.

names.name: The Oak
names.note: English oak; no description.

names.name: βατράχιον
names.note: Several kinds with one acrid ulcerating power; Ranunculus certain, species several.

names.name: Crowfoot
names.note: Many crowfoots; the most common, with acrid blistering leaves and bright yellow flowers, fits R. acris.

names.name: ῥαφάνινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil from radish seed.

names.name: ῥαφανίς
names.note: Garden radish; wild radish (horseradish per some) also treated.

names.name: Wold, Weld, Or Dyer’S Weed
names.note: Dyer's weed, rosette of narrow leaves.

names.name: φύτευμα
names.note: Strouthion-like leaves, many perforated fruits, love charm; Reseda phyteuma named from it.

names.name: σησαμοειδὲς τὸ μέγα
names.note: Fraas: Reseda undata; Sprengel: Reseda mediterranea (Berendes); white flower, sesame-like seed.

names.name: λύκιον
names.note: Extract of a thorny box-leaved shrub from Cappadocia/Lycia (Rhamnus spp.); Indian lycium from Berberis.

names.name: κενταύρειον τὸ μέγα
names.note: Walnut-like leaves, tall stem, red root; standard Centaurea centaurium (now Rhaponticoides).

names.name: ῥᾶ
names.note: Rha from beyond the Bosporus; Berendes 'Rhapontik'; exact Rheum species debated.

names.name: Rhubarb, Or Rephontic
names.note: Garden-grown rhubarb in England with huge round sour leaves: rhapontic.

names.name: Rattle Grass
names.note: Yellow rattle (cock's-comb leaves) and red rattle (lousewort) both described.

names.name: Ῥοδία ῥίζα
names.note: Macedonian root smelling of roses when rubbed; roseroot.

names.name: ῥοῦς
names.note: Culinary rhous from the tanners' sumac shrub, serrate leaves, clustered fruit; standard.

names.name: Gooseberry Bush
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: κίκινον ἔλαιον
names.note: Oil pressed from kroton (castor) seeds; standard.

names.name: κίκι
names.note: Kroton, seed like a tick, oil for lamps; Berendes: Ricinus communis; uncontroversial.

names.name: ἀργεμώνη
names.note: Papaver argemone (= Roemeria argemone): wild-poppy-like, scarlet flower, elongated capsule; text also has RV 'argemone hetera'.

names.name: ῥόδινον
names.note: Rose petals steeped in oil with aromatic stypsis; rose species not specified.

names.name: ῥοδίτης δὲ οὕτω σκευάζεται
names.note: Dried roses (rhodon) in must; ancient rose usually read as Rosa gallica/damascena group.

names.name: Roses
names.note: Garden roses (red, white, damask) and briar roses collectively.

names.name: κυνόσβατος
names.note: Tree-like thorny shrub, white flower, oblong red fruit woolly inside: wild rose (dog rose standard).

names.name: ῥόδα
names.note: Rose petals for juice and pastilles; ancient garden rose usually read as R. gallica/damascena group.

names.name: βάτος
names.note: Common bramble; Greek species probably Rubus sanctus/ulmifolius.

names.name: The Bramble, Or Black-Berry Bush
names.note: Bramble/blackberry, aggregate species.

names.name: βάτος Ἰδαία
names.note: Idaean bramble, much softer with small spines; raspberry.

names.name: λάπαθον
names.note: Four kinds: marsh oxylapathon, garden, small wild, and oxalis (sorrel); all docks.

names.name: Dock
names.note: All docks treated together; red dock/bloodwort and yellow dock named.

names.name: Sorrel
names.note: Ordinary sorrel of gardens and fields.

names.name: Great Round-Leaved Dock, Or Bastard Rhubarb
names.note: Large round leaves, yellow root resembling rhubarb: alpine dock.

names.name: βρεττανική
names.note: Dark, hairy, astringent dock-like leaves; Pliny's britannica, usually a water dock; uncertain.

names.name: ἱππολάπαθον
names.note: 'Horse-dock': a large dock of marshes; species uncertain.

names.name: Garden-Patience, Or Monk’S Rhubarb
names.note: Garden patience/monk's rhubarb is Rumex patientia.

names.name: ὑπόγλωσσον
names.note: Myrtle-like 'leaves' with tongue-like outgrowths; Ruscus hypoglossum.

names.name: Ἰδαία ῥίζα
names.note: Leaves like butcher's broom with flowering outgrowths; Ruscus suggested, uncertain.

names.name: δάφνη Ἀλεξάνδρεια
names.note: Berendes: Ruscus hypophyllum; synonyms Danae and Hypoglotton point to related Ruscaceae.

names.name: The Willow Tree
names.note: Willows collectively; no description.

names.name: ἰτέα
names.note: Itea = willow; species not specified, white willow usual reading.

names.name: Αἰθιοπίς
names.note: Woolly phlomos-like leaves, square stem; Salvia aethiopis named from it.

names.name: ἐλελίσφακον
names.note: Elelisphakon: long shrub, square twigs, rough whitish fragrant leaves; Greek sage.

names.name: ἐλελισφακίτης ὁμοίως
names.note: Elelisphakos usually Greek sage Salvia fruticosa (S. triloba).

names.name: Sage
names.note: Garden sage.

names.name: Clary, Or More Properly Clear-Eye
names.note: Garden clary; standard identification.

names.name: Wild Clary
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ὅρμινον
names.note: Cultivated horminon, square stem; Berendes Salvia horminum (= S. viridis); wild kind other Salvia.

names.name: The Dwarf-Elder
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἀκτῆ
names.note: Two kinds: tree elder and herbaceous chamaiakte (dwarf elder, S. ebulus); Berendes.

names.name: The Elder Tree
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Sanicle
names.note: Palmately lobed glossy leaves: wood sanicle.

names.name: Lavender-Cotton
names.note: Lavender-cotton is the standard name of Santolina chamaecyparissus.

names.name: στοιβῆς ὁ καρπὸς
names.note: Stoibe of Greek authors, astringent; usual identification; chapter gives uses only.

names.name: Winter And Summer Savoury
names.note: Summer (S. hortensis) and winter (S. montana) savory.

names.name: θύμβρα
names.note: Berendes Satureja thymbra; cultivated kind perhaps another savory.

names.name: θυμβρίτης ὁμοίως σκευάζεται
names.note: Thymbra = savory, usually Satureja thymbra.

names.name: The Common White Saxifrage
names.note: Small reddish bulbils (kernels) at the root: white meadow saxifrage.

names.name: πυκνόκομον
names.note: Berendes: a Scabiosa, species disputed; Fraas suggests Scabiosa ambrosioides; speculative.

names.name: σκάνδιξ
names.note: Wild bitter pot-herb eaten raw or boiled; standard.

names.name: σκόλυμος
names.note: Spiny head, edible root and shoots; Berendes S. maculatus; artichoke rejected.

names.name: σκορπιοειδές
names.note: Seeds like scorpion tails; Berendes: Scorpiurus sulcata; identification rests on the name.

names.name: Water Betony
names.note: Brown-wort; square stalks, by water-courses; = Scrophularia aquatica of older floras.

names.name: Fig-Wort, Or Throat-Wort
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: γαλήοψις
names.note: Nettle-like, foul-smelling, thin purple flowers, in hedges; Scrophularia or Lamium proposed.

names.name: Rye
names.note: Rye grain.

names.name: ἀείζῳον τὸ μικρόν
names.note: Small aeizoon on walls, rocks, tombs, with umbel of small flowers; stonecrop.

names.name: δοκεῖ δὲ τρίτον
names.note: Telephion/illecebra: broader hairy purslane-like leaves, acrid; Sedum proposed.

names.name: Stone-Crop, Prick-Madam, Or Small-Houseleek
names.note: Trailing stonecrop on walls and roofs; cooling, harmless virtues suggest S. album, not hot wall-pepper.

names.name: κηπαία
names.note: Purslane-like herb with darker leaves; identification rests largely on the name; description too brief.

names.name: Houseleek Or Sengreen
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Saracen’S Confound, Or Saracen’S Woundwort
names.note: Man-high, willow-like toothed leaves, yellow star flowers: Solidago saracenica of herbals.

names.name: λογχῖτις
names.note: Flowers like gaping comic masks with a white tongue-like lip: tongue orchid; species debated.

names.name: σησαμοειδὲς τὸ μικρόν
names.note: Sprengel Reseda canescens (= Sesamoides interrupta), Fraas Aubrieta deltoidea, older Passerina hirsuta (Berendes); speculative.

names.name: σήσαμον κακοστόμαχον καὶ
names.note: Sesamon = sesame; uncontroversial.

names.name: ὀρεοσέλινον
names.note: Rock/mountain umbellifer; Gesner and Sprengel Seseli libanotis, Fraas Seseli annuum.

names.name: σέσελι
names.note: Massilian = Seseli tortuosum; Ethiopian = Bupleurum fruticosum; Peloponnesian uncertain (Berendes).

names.name: καὶ ἡ ἔλυμος
names.note: Elymos/meline, a millet-like cereal; usually identified as foxtail millet.

names.name: σιδηρῖτις
names.note: Horehound-like leaves, square stems, whorls with black seed; wound herb; species uncertain.

names.name: λυχνὶς στεφανωματική
names.note: Garland lychnis, purple leukoion-like flower; Berendes Lychnis coronaria.

names.name: ὠκιμοειδές
names.note: Basil-like leaves, henbane-like capsules with black seed; Caryophyllaceae, species debated.

names.name: Campion, Wild
names.note: Wild white campion described; red wild campion = Silene dioica.

names.name: μήκων ἀφρώδης
names.note: Small white 'foamy' plant with emetic seed; Silene proposed (Berendes); uncertain.

names.name: σίλλυβον
names.note: Broad thistle eaten young with oil and salt; Berendes: Mariendistel; name kept in Silybum.

names.name: Our Lady’S Thistle
names.note: White-veined prickly leaves: our lady's thistle.

names.name: λαμψάνη
names.note: Wild pot-herb more nourishing than dock; glossed charlock (LSJ), Linnaeus' Lapsana borrowed the name.

names.name: σίνων
names.note: Syrian celery-like black seed; traditional identification Sison amomum.

names.name: The Hedge-Mustard
names.note: Tough branched stalk, runcinate leaves: hedge mustard.

names.name: ἐρύσιμον
names.note: Berendes: Sisymbrium polyceratium or S. irio; urban weed with horn-like pods, yellow flowers.

names.name: σίσαρον
names.note: Known root vegetable eaten boiled; skirret per standard glossaries, parsnip alternative.

names.name: σμῖλαξ τραχεῖα
names.note: Prickly climber with red grape-like berries; Berendes: Smilax aspera.

names.name: σμύρνιον
names.note: Cilician 'petroselinon' of Amanus, myrrh-tasting seed; Berendes S. perfoliatum.

names.name: Amara Dulcis
names.note: Names Bitter-sweet, Woody Night-shade, Felon-wort; standard identification.

names.name: Golden Rod
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: σπαργάνιον
names.note: Xiphion-like narrower leaves, spherical burs on the stem; bur-reed.

names.name: σπαρτίον
names.note: Leafless tough rods for tying vines, pods with lentil-like seeds; Berendes: Pfriemen.

names.name: στάχυς
names.note: Like prasion but longer, whiter leaves; Berendes Stachys germanica (Sibthorp S. palaestina).

names.name: τραγορίγανος
names.note: Sticky broad-leaved kind: Sprengel Stachys glutinosa; slender kind Satureja juliana (Fraas); uncertain.

names.name: Clown’S Woods
names.note: Clown's woundwort (Gerard); standard identification.

names.name: σταφὶς ἀγρία
names.note: Stavesacre (Delphinium staphisagria = Staphisagria macrosperma); vine-like divided leaves, acrid seeds; standard identification.

names.name: Crab’S Claws
names.note: Fresh-water soldier/water sengreen, Lincolnshire fens; standard identification.

names.name: στύραξ
names.note: Resin of a quince-like tree from Pisidia/Cilicia: Styrax officinalis (standard).

names.name: Devil’S-Bit
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: μυρίκη
names.note: Wild tamarisk by lakes; cultivated Egyptian/Syrian kind with gall-like 'fruit' probably T. aphylla. Species not determinable.

names.name: The Tamarisk Tree
names.note: No description; tamarisk of western Europe.

names.name: Costmary, Or Alcost, Or Balsam Herb
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: Garden Tansy
names.note: Garden tansy.

names.name: Dandelion, Vulgarly Called Piss-A-Beds
names.note: Standard identification (aggregate).

names.name: σμῖλαξ
names.note: Romans call it taxus; fir-like tree; yew.

names.name: Τεύριον
names.note: Teukrion of Cilicia, chamaedrys-like; Berendes Teucrium flavum.

names.name: πόλιον
names.note: Polion/teuthrion, white small shrub; standard Teucrium polium.

names.name: σκόρδιον
names.note: Skordion of marshy places, garlic-like smell; Berendes Knoblauch-Gamander.

names.name: Wood-Sage
names.note: Wood-sage with hoary square stalks, sage-like leaves.

names.name: Meadow-Rue
names.note: Yellow stringy creeping root, divided leaves: meadow rue.

names.name: θαλίητρον
names.note: Coriander-like leaves, rue-thick stem; meadow-rue.

names.name: θαψία
names.note: Ferula-like umbellifer named from Thapsos; vesicant root; standard identification.

names.name: θύμος
names.note: Berendes Satureja capitata (= Thymbra capitata); purple capitate heads.

names.name: θυμοξάλμῃ ἐχρῶντο οἱ
names.note: Eponymous main ingredient thymos (Thymbra capitata) with salt, barley meal, rue, pennyroyal, vinegar; multi-ingredient.

names.name: θυμίτης
names.note: Thymos usually Thymbra capitata (Coridothymus capitatus).

names.name: ἔρπυλλος
names.note: Garden creeping kind and erect wild kind (zygis); Berendes Thymus serpyllum, T. glabratus.

names.name: Wild Thyme, Or Mother Of Thyme
names.note: Wild/mother of thyme; British plants mostly T. praecox, historically T. serpyllum.

names.name: Thyme
names.note: Garden thyme.

names.name: καυκαλίς
names.note: Span-high hairy umbellifer, fennel-like leaves, white fragrant umbel, eaten; modern Greek kafkalithra = Tordylium apulum; uncertain.

names.name: τόρδιλον
names.note: Cretan seseli of Amanus; round double shield-shaped seed; Berendes T. officinale.

names.name: The Service-Tree
names.note: No description; fruit eaten mellow like medlars; native English service tree (syn. Sorbus torminalis).

names.name: ἄμι
names.note: Tiny oregano-tasting seed; Sprengel Ammi copticum (= ajowan), Fraas Ammi visnaga.

names.name: τραγοπώγων
names.note: Berendes: Tragopogon, purple-flowered; long sweet root; crocus-like leaves fit Tragopogon spp.

names.name: τρίβολος
names.note: Land kind is Tribulus terrestris; the aquatic kind is water chestnut, Trapa.

names.name: Pearl Trefoil
names.note: Common trefoil with white pearl-like leaf spot; no further description.

names.name: λαγώπουν
names.note: Hare's-foot, astringent; usual identification; chapter gives uses only.

names.name: Meadow Trefoil, Or Honeysuckles
names.note: Meadow trefoil; red and white honeysuckles.

names.name: λωτὸς ἄγριος
names.note: Libyan clover-like legume with fenugreek-like seed; Trigonella or Melilotus.

names.name: λωτὸς ὁ ἐν
names.note: Garden 'lotus' called trifolion; clover-like legume, species uncertain.

names.name: τήλινον
names.note: Fenugreek (telis) oil with calamus and cyperus.

names.name: καὶ τὸ ἐκ
names.note: Meal of telis (synonyms boukeras, aigokeras) = fenugreek; uncontroversial.

names.name: τριπόλιον
names.note: Tidal seashore plant; sea aster (Aster tripolium).

names.name: κρίμνον
names.note: Coarse meal of zea and wheat; porridge base.

names.name: ὀλύρα
names.note: Same kind as zea but less nourishing; hulled wheat, usually emmer or einkorn.

names.name: ἀθήρα δὲ ἐκ
names.note: Gruel of finely ground zea: hulled wheat, emmer (T. turgidum subsp. dicoccum) or spelt (T. aestivum subsp. spelta); debated.

names.name: τράγος τὸ σχῆμα
names.note: Groats like chondros but chaffier, from zea: emmer or spelt (T. aestivum subsp. spelta); debated.

names.name: ζέα
names.note: Two kinds: 'simple' (one grain, einkorn) and 'dikokkos' (two grains per husk, emmer).

names.name: ὁ δὲ χονδρος
names.note: Groats from 'dikokkos zea', i.e. two-grained emmer (T. turgidum subsp. dicoccum); spelt (T. aestivum subsp. spelta) possible.

names.name: τύφη
names.note: Typhe of marshes with dense fluffy spike; Berendes Typha angustifolia.

names.name: The Furze Bush
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: βρύον θαλάσσιον
names.note: Thin, lettuce-like, stemless growth on seaside stones; green alga Ulva.

names.name: Nettles
names.note: Stinging nettles; both common and small nettle covered.

names.name: ἀκαλήφη
names.note: Two nettles; wilder kind with flax-like seed is U. pilulifera, other U. urens.

names.name: βρύον
names.note: Fragrant growth on cedar, white poplar and oak: epiphytic lichens (Berendes: Usnea, Parmelia).

names.name: Bilberries, Called By Some Whorts, And Whortle-Berries
names.note: Bilberries/whortleberries; standard identification.

names.name: ἀκακία
names.note: Juice from pods of an Egyptian thorny tree with white flowers and lupin-like pods: Acacia (Vachellia) nilotica.

names.name: νάρδος Κελτική
names.note: Alpine 'saliunca' of Liguria and Istria: Valeriana celtica (standard).

names.name: νάρδος ὀρεινή
names.note: Berendes: Valeriana tuberosa; black fragrant asphodel-like root tubers. Description defective (no flower), so debated.

names.name: ἐλλέβορος λευκός
names.note: Plantain-like leaves; emetic root; Roman synonym Veratrum album; uncontroversial.

names.name: φλόμος
names.note: Several white and black phlomos kinds; mullein, Phlomis among the wild kinds.

names.name: Mullein
names.note: Common white mullein with woolly leaves, tall stalk.

names.name: ἱερὰ βοτάνη
names.note: Hiera botane: angular jointed stems, oak-like leaves; vervain; species split between 4.59/4.60 debated.

names.name: Brook Lime, Or Water-Pimpernel
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: ἀφάκη
names.note: Berendes: Vicia cracca, rejecting Lathyrus aphaca. Chapter text also contains the leek chapter (2.149 πράσον).

names.name: ὄροβος
names.note: Narrow-leaved small plant with podded seed yielding orobinon flour; standard.

names.name: φακός
names.note: Lentil; standard.

names.name: σμῖλαξ κηπαία
names.note: Twining pulse with kidney-shaped seeds; Berendes' Phaseolus vulgaris is New World, so Old World cowpea preferred.

names.name: κληματίς
names.note: Bay- or myrtle-like leaves on trailing stems; periwinkle per Berendes/Beck.

names.name: Periwinkle
names.note: Trailing rooting stems, small shiny leaves, pale blue flowers in woods.

names.name: ἀσκληπιάς
names.note: Ivy-like leaves, fragrant roots; traditional Vincetoxicum, Fraas 'Asclepias Dioscoridis'.

names.name: κιρκαία
names.note: Berendes: not determined; Anguillara Cynanchum nigrum, Lobelius Circaea lutetiana.

names.name: Heart’S-Ease
names.note: Standard identification.

names.name: γιγγίδιον
names.note: Wild-carrot-like bitter Syrian/Cilician pot-herb; equated with Daucus gingidium/Ammi visnaga; uncertain.

names.name: ἄγνος
names.note: Agnos or lygos: riverside shrub, olive-like leaves, purple/white flowers; standard.

names.name: στρύχνον ὑπνωτικόν
names.note: Sleep-inducing strychnos with red fruit in husk; Withania (Berendes, Beck).

names.name: ξάνθιον
names.note: Burr-fruited weed of lake beds, used to dye hair blond; name preserved in Xanthium.

names.name: ζιγγίβερι
names.note: Ginger rhizome; uncontroversial despite Dioscorides' Troglodytic/Arabian provenance.

names.name: πολύκνημον
names.note: Oregano-like leaves, jointed stem, no umbel; Fraas Ziziphora capitata; uncertain.
